reports.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Terremoto - Campamentos Transitorios: 1 Catia La Mar (02/08/2026)
Situation Report No.8: Earthquakes in Venezuela 2026 (M7.2 and M7.5), 30 July 2026
reports.body_text:
**HIGHLIGHTS**

• More than a month after the two earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, the emergency response remains active while laying the groundwork for early recovery. Priorities now center on sustaining essential health services, strengthening referral pathways, and supporting temporary camps, while preventing public health risks and ensuring the continuous, needs-based supply of medicines and essential equipment.

• Integrated surveillance continues to strengthen early detection and public health risk monitoring across affected areas. Approximately 30,638 vaccine doses have been administered, while laboratory, environmental and event-based surveillance activities continue supporting timely verification and response.

• Transitional camps now shelter 24,477 people across 107 sites at 87% occupancy, with health, WASH, and protection needs extending beyond La Guaira toward Distrito Capital and Miranda as populations move, requiring coordinated action across multiple states.

• PAHO/WHO continued supporting the response with critical medicines and equipment, benefiting 29 actors through its supplies and donations to date, and facilitated logistical support for 11 accepted donor offers. The latest delivery equipped four health facilities in La Guaira—extending primary care to 40,000 people—and delivered WASH items ensuring safe water for 800 families and nearly 110,000 people per month.

• PAHO/WHO continues strengthening the Ministry of Popular Power for Health (MPPS) through its Regional Response Team across emergency coordination, logistics, information management, epidemiology, laboratory, WASH, immunization, risk communication, and EMT coordination, with additional experts arriving for entomology, infection prevention and control. It also supports the virtual CICOM and EMT mobilization, with ten teams now operational across La Guaira, Caracas, Miranda, while the EMT Network reinforces the Ministry's epidemiological surveillance and early detection in affected areas

reports.title: PAHO Regional Situation Report No.8: Measles in the Region of the Americas (31 July 2026)
reports.body_text:
**Situation Overview**

Between epidemiological week (EW) 1 and EW 29 of 2026 (ending on 25 July 2026), the Region of the Americas reported 47,026 confirmed measles cases from 17 countries and territories, representing approximately a 5-fold increase compared to the same period in 2025. Guatemala (30,040), Mexico (12,233), the United States (2,318) and Canada (1,107) accounted for the majority (97%) of confirmed cases. Additionally, 48 deaths have been reported. The increase in the regional cumulative total compared with Situation Report No.7 is primarily attributable to Guatemala, which remains the major contributor of newly confirmed cases with 1395 added cases, followed by additional cases reported by Mexico with 119 added cases, Peru with 93 added cases, the United States with 77 added cases, Canada with 9 added cases, Bolivia with 3 added cases and Colombia with 1 added case.

During EW 27 and EW 28 of 2026, the Region of the Americas reported 1,697 new confirmed measles cases across seven countries and territories, representing a 6.7% decrease compared with the previous two-week period (EW 25-26; 1,818 new cases)2 (Figure 1). The decrease was driven mainly by fewer cases reported in Guatemala after the retrospective update was incorporated in the previous situation report.

Following the earthquakes, while the risk of measles introduction and spread in Venezuela remains a concern, there have been no confirmed cases reported in the country thus far.

reports.title: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 31 de julio 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**CIFRAS CLAVE**

- 3,4M de personas necesitan asistencia alimentaria humanitaria en Venezuela
- 3,4M de personas podrían enfrentarse a niveles de inseguridad alimentaria de crisis (CIF 3) o emergencia (CIF 4) en Haití
- 9,7K personas permanecen aisladas en Coquimbo, Chile, debido a fuertes tormentas

**VENEZUELA: TERREMOTO**

Las necesidades humanitarias siguen elevadas en Venezuela tras los terremotos del 24 de junio, ya que los hogares afectados continúan recuperándose de desplazamientos, pérdidas de medios de vida e interrupciones en el acceso a alimentos. La Red de Sistemas de Alerta Temprana contra la Hambruna (FEWS NET) estima que entre 3,0 y 3,49 millones de personas necesitan asistencia alimentaria humanitaria, y que el terremoto ha provocado resultados de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en los estados más afectados. Las evaluaciones rápidas indican que muchas familias afectadas han reducido el consumo de alimentos, incluyendo la reducción de las porciones y el salto de comidas para priorizar a los niños. Los socios humanitarios continúan ampliando la asistencia, con el PMA alcanzando a más de 120.000 personas a través de comidas calientes, cestas de alimentos, raciones listas para comer y vales electrónicos. A pesar de la respuesta en curso, persisten importantes necesidades de seguridad alimentaria mientras los hogares reconstruyen sus medios de vida y el acceso a los mercados y servicios básicos sigue siendo limitado.

**CHILE: LLUVIAS INTENSAS**

Las operaciones de respuesta continúan en Chile tras el clima severo que comenzó a mediados de julio, mientras que un nuevo sistema frontal trae riesgos adicionales de lluvias e inundaciones en varias regiones. Las autoridades han emitido nuevas alertas rojas en partes de Ñuble, Biobío y otras zonas afectadas debido al aumento del nivel de los ríos y a los riesgos de inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra. En Coquimbo, más de 9.700 personas permanecen aisladas. El Gobierno también ha declarado una emergencia agrícola en Atacama, Coquimbo y Valparaíso para apoyar los medios de vida afectados, mientras las autoridades continúan los esfuerzos para restaurar infraestructuras, reconectar comunidades aisladas y abordar los impactos de una de las emergencias meteorológicas más severas que han afectado al país en décadas.

**REGIONAL: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA**

La seguridad alimentaria sigue bajo presión en las zonas vulnerables de Centroamérica y Colombia. En Centroamérica, se prevé que persistan las condiciones de crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en el Corredor Seco y en partes de Alta Verapaz y las Altiplano Occidental de Guatemala, donde las pérdidas de cosechas, el agotamiento de las reservas de alimentos y los ingresos por debajo de la media han aumentado la dependencia de estrategias negativas de afrontamiento. La Red de Sistemas de Alerta Temprana contra la Hambruna (FEWS NET) estima que entre 2,0 y 2,49 millones de personas en Guatemala necesitarán asistencia alimentaria entre junio y septiembre. En Colombia, se prevé que persistan las condiciones de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) en La Guajira y Chocó, donde sequías, inundaciones, inseguridad y precios elevados limitan la producción agrícola, los ingresos y el acceso al mercado. Se prevé que las condiciones de El Niño reduzcan aún más las lluvias y las oportunidades laborales agrícolas, aunque las cosechas estacionales y el empleo a partir de octubre deberían suponer alguna mejora.

**HAITÍ: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA**

Entre junio de 2026 y enero de 2027, se prevé que entre 3,0 y 3,49 millones de personas enfrenten niveles de inseguridad alimentaria de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) o Emergencia (Fase 4 de la CIF) en Haití. La violencia persistente sigue afectando los medios de vida, la producción agrícola, los mercados y las rutas comerciales, generando altos costos de transporte y limitando el acceso a los alimentos. Se prevé que los resultados de Emergencia (Fase 4 de la CIF) persistan entre las personas desplazadas internamente y los hogares muy pobres. Aunque las cosechas de primavera pueden mejorar temporalmente el acceso a los alimentos, las zonas cultivadas siguen por debajo de la media, la inflación sigue elevada en el 21% y la intensificación prevista de las condiciones de El Niño amenaza con nuevos déficits de lluvia y cosechas por debajo de la media más adelante en 2026, sosteniendo altas necesidades humanitarias hasta principios de 2027.

reports.title: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 31 July 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**KEY FIGURES**

- 3.4M people require humanitarian food assistance in Venezuela
- 3.4M people could face crisis (IPC 3) or emergency (IPC 4) hunger in Haiti
- 9.7K people remain isolated in Coquimbo, Chile due to severe storms

**VENEZUELA: EARTHQUAKE**

Humanitarian needs remain elevated in Venezuela following the 24 June earthquakes, as affected households continue to recover from displacement, livelihood losses, and disrupted access to food. The Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) estimates that 3.0 to 3.49 million people require humanitarian food assistance, with the earthquake driving Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes across the most affected states. Rapid assessments indicate that many impacted families have reduced food consumption, including cutting meal portions and skipping meals to prioritize children. Humanitarian partners continue to scale up assistance, with WFP reaching more than 120,000 people through hot meals, food baskets, ready-to-eat rations, and electronic vouchers. Despite the ongoing response, significant food security needs persist as households rebuild livelihoods and access to markets and basic services remains constrained.

**CHILE: HEAVY RAINFALL**

Response operations continue in Chile following the severe weather that began in mid-July, while a new frontal system brings additional rainfall and flood risks across several regions. Authorities have issued new red alerts in parts of Ñuble, Biobío and other affected areas due to rising river levels, flooding and landslide risks. In Coquimbo, more than 9,700 people remain isolated. The Government has also declared an agricultural emergency in Atacama, Coquimbo and Valparaíso to support affected livelihoods, as authorities continue efforts to restore infrastructure, reconnect isolated communities and address the impacts of one of the most severe weather emergencies to affect the country in decades.

**REGIONAL: FOOD SECURITY**

Food security remains under pressure across vulnerable areas of Central America and Colombia. In Central America, Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected to persist in the Dry Corridor and parts of Alta Verapaz and the Western Highlands in Guatemala, where crop losses, depleted food stocks, and below-average incomes have increased reliance on negative coping strategies. The Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) estimates that 2.0 to 2.49 million people in Guatemala will require food assistance between June and September. In Colombia, Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected to continue in La Guajira and Chocó, where drought, flooding, insecurity, and elevated prices are constraining agricultural production, incomes, and market access. El Niño conditions are expected to further reduce rainfall and agricultural labour opportunities, although seasonal harvests and employment from October onward should provide some improvement.

**HAITI: FOOD SECURITY**

Between June 2026 and January 2027, 3.0 to 3.49 million people are expected to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels of food insecurity in Haiti, according to FEWS NET. Persistent violence continues to disrupt livelihoods, agricultural production, markets, and trade routes, driving high transportation costs and limiting food access. Emergency (IPC Phase 4) outcomes are expected to persist among internally displaced persons and very poor households Although spring harvests may temporarily improve food access, cultivated areas remain below average, inflation remains elevated at 21 percent, and the anticipated intensification of El Niño conditions threatens additional rainfall deficits and below-average harvests later in 2026, sustaining high humanitarian needs through early 2027.

- Hasta el 24 de julio, las autoridades reportaron **5.546 personas**  
    **fallecidas y 16.740 heridas a causa de los terremotos.**
- El Sistema de las Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias continúan ampliando la respuesta multisectorial a la emergencia. Para atender las necesidades de **1,3 millones de personas afectadas durante los próximos seis meses.**

**Situación general**

Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos el 24 de junio (18:00, hora local) en la región centro-norte. El primer sismo, de magnitud 7,2, tuvo su epicentro en el eje San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán (Yaracuy/Carabobo). De acuerdo con una actualización reciente del Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS), el segundo sismo, de magnitud 7,5, tuvo su epicentro a 17 kilómetros al oeste de Catia La Mar, frente a las costas del estado La Guaira. **Al 24 de julio, las autoridades reportan 1.500 réplicas.**

La respuesta gubernamental continúa centrada en la atención de la población afectada y la gestión de los campamentos transitorios. Más de un mes después de los terremotos, la respuesta humanitaria continúa ampliándose en los estados afectados. **Al 30 de julio, más de 207.700 personas accedieron a servicios esenciales** y asistencia humanitaria a través del trabajo conjunto de comunidades, organizaciones humanitarias, entidades de las Naciones Unidas, socios donantes y autoridades.

**Nota**

> **El informe se publicará de manera semanal. reports.body_text:
**Situation Report No. 31**  
**Earthquakes in Venezuela**  
**31 July 2026**  
**Time: 5:00 pm**

**Highlights**

- **More than 207,700 people affected by the earthquakes** have received humanitarian assistance and essential services through a coordinated multi-sector response involving humanitarian organizations, United Nations agencies, communities, and national and local authorities.
- As of 24 July, **authorities reported 5,546 deaths and 16,740 injuries** as a result of the earthquakes.
- The United Nations system and its partner organizations continue scaling up the multisectoral response to the emergency. To address the needs of **1.3 million people affected by the earthquakes over the next six months.**

**Situation overview**

Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive major earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5) that struck the country's north-central region on 24 June (18:00 local time). The first earthquake, measuring 7.2, was centered along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis (Yaracuy/Carabobo). According to a recent update from the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the second earthquake, measuring 7.5, had its epicenter 17 kilometers west of Catia La Mar, off the coast of La Guaira State. **As of 24 July, authorities reported 1,500 aftershocks.**

As of 24 July, authorities reported **5,546 deaths and 16,740 injuries resulting from the earthquakes.** They also reported that 17,907 people lost their homes, while 856 buildings were affected, including 190 that collapsed. A preliminary assessment by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct damage to housing and infrastructure at approximately **US$37 billion,** while preliminary estimates from UNDP place direct physical damages at US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 per cent of GDP.

The government response continues to focus on assisting affected populations and managing temporary displacement sites. According to authorities, **107 temporary camps remain operational, with a capacity for 28,223 people** **and a current occupancy of 24,477 people.** Of those accommodated, 12,752 people are in **La Guaira**, 9,092 in the **Capital District**, 1,958 in **Miranda**, and 675 in **Aragua**.

More than one month after the earthquakes, the humanitarian response continues to expand across the affected states. **As of 30 July, more than 207,700 people had access to essential services and humanitarian assistance** through the joint efforts of communities, humanitarian organizations, United Nations entities, donor partners, and national and local authorities.

**Note**

> ***The report will be published on a weekly basis. We thank partner organizations, United Nations entities and donors for their valuable contributions, and encourage them to continue reporting their earthquake response activities through the 345W platform. For more information on reporting and the use of the tool, please refer to the presentation:*** [***345W Preparedness and Response***](https://drive.google.com/file/d/12Tdck_8iHPTcj6BRDeYMwkp1lwS_-rYq/view?usp=sharing)

reports.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #18 (28 al 30 de julio 2026)
reports.body_text:
El Reporte de Situación No. 18 presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela y cubre el período comprendido entre el 28 y el 30 de julio de 2026.

## Aspectos destacados

Entre el 28 y el 30 de julio, la OIM continuó su respuesta multisectorial en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas mediante intervenciones en alojamiento y coordinación y gestión de campamentos, salud, protección, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH) y gestión de información.

A la fecha, la OIM y Fundación Vivienda Popular han proporcionado **4.627 sets de cocina, 4.232 lonas plásticas, 3.148 lámparas solares, 2.990 bidones plegables, 2.345 baldes, 2.210 kits de higiene, 947 mosquiteros y 821 kits de refugio** a familias afectadas por los terremotos.

Los equipos apoyados por la OIM han brindado **7.374 consultas médicas a 6.565 personas afectadas por los terremotos** mediante servicios de salud, salud mental y apoyo psicológico en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas.

## Actividades de la OIM

La OIM continuó la cogestión de cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira: Campo de Golf, Mare Abajo II, Polideportivo José María Vargas, Playa Grande y César Nieves, apoyando la prestación de servicios, el registro de población, la orientación comunitaria y la coordinación operativa.

En Campo de Golf continuaron los avances en la puesta en funcionamiento de la herradura de servicios, la instalación de iluminación solar, la adecuación de un espacio amigable y mejoras de infraestructura. En Mare Abajo II se actualizó el mapeo de servicios y avanzaron los preparativos para distribuciones coordinadas. En César Nieves y Playa Grande, la OIM continuó apoyando la coordinación de servicios, el seguimiento de infraestructura y el monitoreo de movimientos de población.

Durante el período, la OIM y Fundación Vivienda Popular proporcionaron **491 lonas plásticas, 491 sets de cocina y 54 baldes** a familias afectadas por los terremotos.

En WASH, la OIM continuó ampliando el acceso a servicios de agua segura, saneamiento e higiene mediante actividades de monitoreo de calidad del agua, mejoras de drenaje, gestión de residuos y apoyo a infraestructura sanitaria. A la fecha, la OIM ha proporcionado **2.990 bidones plegables, 284 bidones semiplegables de 10 litros y 2.210 kits de higiene**.

La OIM y su socio implementador Ven Da Tu Mano continuaron prestando servicios de salud, salud mental y apoyo psicológico mediante equipos móviles. Durante el período, se realizaron más de **160 consultas de salud y salud mental** en el Polideportivo José María Vargas.

La OIM continuó apoyando el registro y la actualización de información a través del Sistema Unificado de Gestión de Información (IMS) en los cinco campamentos transitorios administrados por Naciones Unidas. También avanzaron las actividades de recopilación de información en asentamientos comunitarios del municipio Zamora, estado Miranda. Asimismo, continuaron los preparativos para la evaluación de asentamientos informales y el monitoreo de movilidad mediante la Matriz de Seguimiento de Desplazamiento (DTM).

En protección, la OIM continuó brindando servicios de información, asistencia legal, gestión de casos, actividades de protección infantil, prevención de la trata de personas y mecanismos de retroalimentación comunitaria. Las actividades incluyeron el fortalecimiento de rutas de derivación, actividades comunitarias y acciones de sensibilización realizadas en el marco del Día Mundial contra la Trata de Personas. A la fecha, **207 personas han recibido asistencia individualizada de protección** mediante servicios apoyados por la OIM.

Como colíder del Grupo de Trabajo de Infraestructura y Alojamientos Temporales junto con ACNUR, la OIM continuó apoyando la coordinación operativa, el mapeo de servicios, la gestión de información y la planificación conjunta en los campamentos transitorios.

## Respuesta planificada de la OIM

La OIM continuará fortaleciendo la infraestructura, la prestación de servicios, las intervenciones WASH, el apoyo en alojamiento y las actividades de coordinación y gestión de campamentos en los campamentos transitorios.

Asimismo, continuará prestando servicios de salud, salud mental, apoyo psicológico y protección, fortaleciendo al mismo tiempo las rutas de derivación para asistencia especializada.

Además, la OIM mantendrá el monitoreo de movilidad, las actividades de registro, la gestión de información, las evaluaciones en asentamientos comunitarios y la coordinación con autoridades y organizaciones implementadoras para respaldar la planificación de la respuesta basada en evidencia.

reports.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #18 (28 to 30 July 2026)
reports.body_text:
The eighteenth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, covering the period from 28 to 30 July 2026.

## Highlights

Between 28 and 30 July, IOM continued its multisectoral response in temporary accommodation sites and affected communities through interventions in shelter and camp coordination and management, health, protection, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and information management.

To date, IOM and Fundación Vivienda Popular have provided **4,627 kitchen sets, 4,232 plastic tarpaulins, 3,148 solar lamps, 2,990 collapsible water containers, 2,345 buckets, 2,210 hygiene kits, 947 mosquito nets and 821 shelter kits** to earthquake-affected families.

IOM-supported teams have delivered **7,374 medical consultations to 6,565 earthquake-affected people** through health, mental health and psychological support services in temporary accommodation sites and affected communities.

## IOM Activities

IOM continued co-managing five temporary accommodation sites in La Guaira: Campo de Golf, Mare Abajo II, José María Vargas Sports Complex, Playa Grande and César Nieves, supporting service delivery, population registration, community information services and operational coordination.

At Campo de Golf, progress continued on the centralized service hub, installation of solar lighting, establishment of a child-friendly space and infrastructure improvements. At Mare Abajo II, service mapping was updated and preparations advanced for coordinated distributions. In César Nieves and Playa Grande, IOM continued supporting service coordination, infrastructure monitoring and population movement follow-up.

During the reporting period, IOM and Fundación Vivienda Popular provided **491 plastic tarpaulins, 491 kitchen sets and 54 buckets** to earthquake-affected families.

In WASH, IOM continued expanding access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services through water quality monitoring, drainage improvements, waste management and sanitation infrastructure support. To date, IOM has provided **2,990 collapsible water containers, 284 semi-collapsible 10-liter water containers and 2,210 hygiene kits**.

IOM and its implementing partner Ven Da Tu Mano continued delivering health, mental health and psychological support services through mobile teams. During the reporting period, more than **160 health and mental health consultations** were provided at José María Vargas Sports Complex.

IOM continued supporting registration and information updates through the unified Information Management System (IMS) across the five temporary accommodation sites and advanced information collection activities in community settlements in Zamora Municipality, Miranda State. Preparations also continued for informal settlement assessments and mobility monitoring through the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM).

In protection, IOM continued providing information services, legal assistance, case management, child protection activities, trafficking in persons prevention and community feedback mechanisms. Activities included strengthening referral pathways, community outreach and awareness activities conducted in connection with World Day Against Trafficking in Persons. To date, **207 individuals have received individualized protection assistance** through IOM-supported services.

As co-lead of the Infrastructure and Temporary Accommodation Working Group together with UNHCR, IOM continued supporting operational coordination, service mapping, information management and joint planning across temporary accommodation sites.

## IOM Planned Response

IOM will continue strengthening infrastructure, service delivery, WASH interventions, shelter support and camp coordination and management activities in temporary accommodation sites.

IOM will also continue delivering health, mental health, psychological support and protection services while strengthening referral pathways for specialized assistance.

In addition, IOM will maintain mobility monitoring, registration activities, information management, community settlement assessments and coordination with authorities and implementing organizations to support evidence-based response planning.

reports.title: Venezuela: The IRC and the European Union strengthen health and protection response following earthquakes
reports.body_text:
- The response is expected to reach more than 26,000 people.
- Funded by the European Union with €1 million, the intervention will run from July to December 2026.
- Health, protection, and psychosocial support services will be implemented in Miranda, La Guaira, and Caracas.
- The IRC will launch InfoPalante to provide verified information, personalized guidance, and access to safe services.

**Caracas, Venezuela, July 31, 2026 —** One month after the devastating twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, over 5,500 people have been killed and 16,740 injured.

As soon as the earthquakes hit, the European Union partnered with the International Rescue Committee (IRC) to expand essential health and protection services for over 26,000 people affected by the crisis, through a €1 million grant (July–December) from the EU’s Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO).

*"The earthquakes have devastated entire communities, leaving many families without access to healthcare, protection, and other essential services needed to rebuild their lives. The European Union's vital support, together with the unwavering commitment of our partners on the ground, allows us to rapidly scale up lifesaving services and reach those at greatest risk. This intervention will enable us to stand with the people of Venezuela in the face of unimaginable loss and help communities move toward a safe, dignified, and hopeful recovery,"* **said Nicole Kast, IRC Country Director for Colombia, Venezuela, and Ecuador.**

Before the earthquakes, close to eight million people already required humanitarian assistance. Just four weeks later, that [number has grown by 1.4 million](https://www.rescue.org/press-release/one-month-after-earthquakes-venezuela-risks-spiraling-deeper-crisis). EU Humanitarian Aid funding will bolster IRC’s initial emergency response in the hardest-hit areas of La Guaira, Caracas, and Miranda. The IRC and its partners began launching services immediately after the earthquakes hit, delivering essential supplies, supporting frontline workers and providing first aid and primary health care to between 300 and 400 people every day.

In partnership with the Venezuelan Association of Christian-Oriented Health Services (AVESSOC) and the PALUZ Foundation, the IRC will expand access to primary care, and sexual and reproductive health services in affected communities.

In partnership with the Foundation for Children Deserving Protection (FUNDALA), the IRC will provide psychosocial support and case management for at-risk populations, including survivors of gender-based violence, and distribute dignity kits.

To increase access to vital information, the IRC will launch InfoPalante in Venezuela. Through this digital channel, affected people will be able to access verified information, identify health and protection services and referral pathways and receive personalized, real-time guidance. InfoPalante is part of [Signpost](https://www.signpost.ngo/), a global initiative co-launched by the IRC and Mercy Corps operating around the world that provides reliable and accessible information to people affected by humanitarian emergencies. InfoPalante has been active in Colombia since 2020 and in Ecuador since 2022.

**Media contacts**

Sylvan Foley

**sylvan.foley@rescue.org**

IRC Global Communications

**communications@rescue.org**

reports.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #17 (24 to 27 July 2026)
reports.body_text:
The seventeenth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, covering the period from 24 to 27 July.

## **Highlights**

Between 24 and 27 July, IOM continued its multisectoral response in transitional sites and affected communities through interventions in shelter and site coordination, health, protection, WASH, and information management.

During the reporting period, IOM and its partner Fundación Vivienda Popular distributed **343 tarpaulins, 343 kitchen sets, 343 solar lamps, 618 jerry cans, 275 ropes, 275 blankets, 35 mosquito nets, and 33 buckets**, contributing to improved shelter conditions and access to essential items.

To date, IOM continues supporting the management of five transitional sites in La Guaira, where **4,538 people remain hosted**, through the provision of multisectoral services, coordination, and needs monitoring.

## **IOM Activities**

IOM continued the co-management of five transitional sites in La Guaira, strengthening coordination mechanisms, registration, community participation, and inter-agency coordination. In Campo de Golf, registration of **102 families** was completed and spatial reorganization advanced for the future installation of **100 tents with IsraAID**. In Mare Abajo II, Playa Grande, and César Nieves, infrastructure improvements, registration updates, and transition planning processes continued.

Under WASH, coordination advanced for the installation of a **20,000-litre-per-day water storage and treatment system** in Campo de Golf, alongside sanitation improvements, waste management, and sanitary infrastructure enhancements in other sites. To date, **2,170 collapsible jerry cans, 1,091 hygiene kits, and 93 water storage containers** have been distributed.

IOM and its partner Ven Da Tu Mano continued providing primary health care and **psychological first aid (PFA)** through mobile teams, conducting **more than 500 consultations during the reporting period**, including follow-up and referrals for specialized care. IOM also continued co-leading the **PFA Technical Working Group** with PAHO/WHO to strengthen referral pathways.

Under information management, IOM completed the **DTM Household Survey** in transitional sites. Preliminary findings show that **12% of households reached their current location through progressive movements, 55% reported loss of income during the last month, and 55% indicated they do not feel safe when leaving their accommodation**.

Under protection, IOM continued providing guidance, legal assistance, documentation support, referrals, and actions to prevent violence against women, trafficking in persons, and sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). HIAS joined as an IOM implementing partner to expand protection service coverage, including psychological support, legal counselling, child protection, and safe spaces.

## **Planned IOM Response**

IOM will continue strengthening infrastructure and essential services in transitional sites, as well as coordination mechanisms, information management, and community participation.

IOM will also maintain mobile health and **psychological support services**, strengthen referral pathways, and expand specialized protection services, while continuing site monitoring, needs assessments, and coordination with authorities and humanitarian partners.

reports.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #17 (24 al 27 de julio 2026)
reports.body_text:
El decimoséptimo Reporte de Situación presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela, con información correspondiente al período del 24 al 27 de julio.

## **Aspectos destacados**

Entre el 24 y el 27 de julio, la OIM continuó su respuesta multisectorial en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas mediante intervenciones en alojamiento y coordinación de sitios, salud, protección, WASH y gestión de información.

La OIM y su socio Fundación Vivienda Popular distribuyeron durante el período **343 lonas, 343 sets de cocina, 343 lámparas solares, 618 bidones, 275 cuerdas, 275 mantas, 35 mosquiteros y 33 baldes**, fortaleciendo las condiciones de alojamiento y acceso a bienes esenciales.

A la fecha, la OIM continúa apoyando la gestión de cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira, donde **4.538 personas permanecen alojadas**, mediante la provisión de servicios multisectoriales, coordinación y seguimiento de necesidades.

## **Actividades de la OIM**

La OIM continuó la cogestión de cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira, fortaleciendo mecanismos de coordinación, registro, participación comunitaria y articulación interagencial. En Campo de Golf se completó el registro de **102 familias** y avanzó la reorganización del espacio para la instalación futura de **100 carpas con IsraAID**. En Mare Abajo II, Playa Grande y César Nieves continuaron las acciones de mejora de infraestructura, actualización de registros y planificación de procesos de transición.

En WASH, avanzó la coordinación para la instalación de un sistema de almacenamiento y potabilización de **20.000 litros diarios** en Campo de Golf, junto con mejoras de saneamiento, gestión de residuos e infraestructura sanitaria en otros campamentos. A la fecha, se han distribuido **2.170 bidones plegables, 1.091 kits de higiene y 93 bidones de almacenamiento de agua**.

La OIM y su socio Ven Da Tu Mano continuaron brindando atención primaria en salud y salud mental mediante equipos móviles, con **más de 500 consultas realizadas durante el período**, incluyendo seguimiento y derivación de casos especializados. Asimismo, la OIM continuó codirigiendo el Grupo de Trabajo Técnico de salud mental junto con OPS para fortalecer las rutas de referencia.

En gestión de información, la OIM completó la Encuesta de Hogares DTM en campamentos transitorios. Los resultados preliminares muestran que **12% de los hogares llegó a su ubicación actual por etapas, 55% reportó pérdida de ingresos durante el último mes y 55% manifestó no sentirse seguro al salir del alojamiento**.

En protección, la OIM continuó brindando orientación, asistencia legal, apoyo en documentación, derivaciones y acciones de prevención de violencia contra las mujeres, trata de personas y PEAS. HIAS inició su incorporación como socio implementador para ampliar la cobertura de servicios de protección, incluyendo apoyo psicosocial, asesoría legal, protección infantil y espacios seguros.

## **Respuesta planificada de la OIM**

La OIM continuará fortaleciendo la infraestructura y servicios esenciales en campamentos transitorios, así como los mecanismos de coordinación, gestión de información y participación comunitaria.

Asimismo, mantendrá los servicios móviles de salud y salud mental, fortalecerá las rutas de derivación y ampliará la cobertura de servicios especializados de protección, mientras continúa el monitoreo de campamentos, evaluaciones de necesidades y coordinación con autoridades y socios humanitarios.

reports.title: Un mois après les tremblements de terre au Venezuela, la Croix-Rouge est toujours sur le terrain. | IFRC
sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
reports.body_text:
**Protéger les populations contre les épidémies: la surveillance épidémiologique.**

Un mois après la catastrophe, les principales menaces pour la santé publique ne se trouvent plus sous les décombres. Elles découlent désormais des conditions de vie précaires des familles déplacées, qui n'ont pas un accès garanti à l'eau potable et vivent dans des abris surpeuplés où les installations sanitaires sont insuffisantes.

Des équipes conjointes de la Croix-Rouge espagnole et de la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne mènent des évaluations dans ces zones afin **d'anticiper les risques sanitaires et de détecter précocement les maladies respiratoires et gastro-intestinales.** Nombre de ces problèmes de santé sont directement liés au manque d'hygiène et à la pénurie d'eau potable.

Cette surveillance continue, menée en étroite coordination avec les autorités locales et les organisations partenaires, est essentielle **pour prévenir une crise sanitaire secondaire.**

**Reconnecter les familles**

Lorsque les tremblements de terre ont frappé, d'innombrables familles se sont retrouvées dans l'angoisse, sans aucune nouvelle du sort de leurs proches. L'effondrement des bâtiments et **la coupure des communications** ont aggravé la tragédie, laissant planer l'incertitude déchirante quant au sort d'enfants, de parents ou de frères et sœurs portés disparus.

En réponse, les Sociétés nationales de la Croix-Rouge de onze pays (Argentine, Bolivie, Colombie, Costa Rica, Équateur, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexique, Panama, Paraguay et Uruguay) ont activé leurs services de Rétablissement des liens familiaux (RLF).

Aujourd'hui, **la Croix-Rouge vénézuélienne traite des milliers de demandes de recherche émanant de personnes à la recherche de proches,** tant au Venezuela qu'à l'étranger.

**Un soutien essentiel, souvent invisible**

Dans les tout premiers jours qui ont suivi la catastrophe, la Croix-Rouge colombienne, avec le soutien de la Croix-Rouge allemande, a renforcé les télécommunications opérationnelles en installant des équipements radio et des répéteurs afin d'améliorer la couverture du réseau et la coordination dans les zones prioritaires de recherche et de sauvetage.

La nouvelle antenne, récemment installée, couvre une grande partie de Caracas et de La Guaira et est reliée à des répéteurs supplémentaires qui étendent la couverture jusqu'à Maracay. Cette infrastructure permet **une communication fluide entre les équipes d'intervention déployées** à La Guaira, Caracas et dans les régions environnantes.

**Car, en situation d'urgence, des communications fiables sauvent des vies.**

Au-delà des télécommunications, les équipes de la Croix-Rouge poursuivent les évaluations des dégâts et des besoins, exploitent des unités de traitement de l'eau pour approvisionner les organisations humanitaires et distribuent des kits d'hygiène ainsi que des milliers de litres d'eau potable aux familles touchées.

reports.title: Cruz Roja Española moviliza más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria a Venezuela
reports.body_text:
• Un primer envío de 45,5 toneladas ha salido desde el Centro Logístico de Cruz Roja en Las Palmas, en un vuelo facilitado y financiado por el programa Puente Aéreo Humanitario de la Unión Europea (“EU Humanitarian Air Bridge”).

• Más de 35.000 personas se beneficiarán de la ayuda de este primer envío, compuesto por kits de cocina, mosquiteras, lonas plásticas, y contenedores para almacenamiento de agua segura.

• Al menos durante dos años, Cruz Roja Española seguirá en Venezuela apoyando en la reconstrucción y recuperación de las familias afectadas y de sus medios de vida.

**28 de julio de 2026.** Tras un mes de los terremotos que asolaron Venezuela, Cruz Roja Española continúa apoyando a la población afectada, ahora con la movilización de más de 88 toneladas de ayuda humanitaria, de las que una primera parte (45,5 toneladas) partieron este fin de semana desde Las Palmas de Gran Canarias en un avión fletado y financiado por el programa Puente Aéreo Humanitario de la Unión Europea (“EU Humanitarian Air Bridge”). Gracias al apoyo de la Unión Europea se contribuye a asegurar el acceso a artículos de ayuda humanitaria a las familias afectadas, en este caso, a más de 35.000 personas.

Los artículos movilizados por Cruz Roja Española se componen de 15.600 mosquiteras; 18.650 lámparas solares; 7.800 bidones; 34.187 mantas; 10.700 lonas de plástico; 7.124 kits de cocina; 8.714 filtros de agua; 7.852 kits higiene hombres; 10.616 kits higiene mujeres; 2.332 kits de higiene niñas y niños; 8.000.000 pastillas de cloro; 1 ambulancia; 1 minibús; 2 vehículos 4x4 y ordenadores portátiles.

**Un mes de respuestas**

La primera respuesta de Cruz Roja Española frente a los terremotos fue el despliegue de una clínica de emergencia, que se encuentra operativa en La Guaira, con una capacidad de asistencia para 30.000 personas, desde la que ya se ha prestado **atención sanitaria a más de 3.000 personas, de las que más de 500 han recibido atención psicosocial.**

Durante los primeros cuatro meses esta clínica será gestionada por el personal de Cruz Roja Española, con apoyo de personal técnico especializado de Cruz Roja Venezolana, a quien será transferida para dar continuidad a los servicios de salud. La transferencia de servicio será clave para asegurar una atención médica continuada, apoyo psicosocial y prevención de enfermedades, en apoyo y complementariedad a los servicios de salud que han sido afectados.

Desde Cruz Roja Española se sigue apoyando a la Cruz Roja Venezolana en la respuesta conjunta a las necesidades humanitarias más urgentes de las personas y familias afectadas por los terremotos, en coordinación con la Federación Internacional de Sociedades de Cruz Roja y Media Luna Roja.

**Cruz Roja seguirá en Venezuela**

La **presencia de Cruz Roja Española en Venezuela** no finaliza con la cobertura de esta primera fase de emergencia, sino que continuará al menos durante **dos años más,** articulando respuestas en diferentes áreas clave de intervención: **despliegue de personal especializado**; **envío y distribución de artículos de primera necesidad**; respuesta integral en **salud**; **recuperación de medios de vida** y protección y **fortalecimiento de capacidades operativas** de Cruz Roja Venezolana.

Los pasos más inmediatos serán, en el ámbito de la salud, la transferencia de la clínica de emergencia a la Cruz Roja Venezolana, y el apoyo para el restablecimiento de los servicios del Centro Hospitalario de San José, afectados por los terremotos.

En el marco de la fase de recuperación y con el objetivo de dar respuesta a las personas que han perdido sus medios de vida, se están identificando acciones para contribuir al restablecimiento seguro y digno de las condiciones de vida de las familias y comunidades afectadas por el terremoto, facilitando el acceso a servicios básicos, medios de vida y vivienda segura.

Las 19 personas delegadas de Cruz Roja Española actualmente desplegadas en el país siguen trabajando en la respuesta humanitaria urgente, así como en la identificación de acciones de recuperación temprana.

**Sobre Cruz Roja Española**

Cruz Roja Española pertenece al mayor movimiento humanitario del mundo. Colabora con entidades públicas y privadas para que la ayuda llegue a todas las personas que lo necesitan, en cualquier lugar y en el momento oportuno. Su misión es prevenir y aliviar el sufrimiento humano, proteger la vida y la salud y hacer respetar a las personas.

Sus más de 231.000 personas voluntarias dan respuesta en 1.263 municipios, lo que permite atender anualmente a más de 11,6 millones de personas en los ámbitos nacional e internacional. Todo ello con el apoyo de cerca de 1,3 millones de personas socias, empresas y alianzas en todos los sectores de la sociedad.

Cruz Roja Española ha puesto en marcha un Plan de Respuesta para hacer frente a los efectos de la DANA, con una ejecución continuada a tres años que tiene como objetivo principal contribuir a la recuperación, la construcción de resiliencia y el bienestar físico, emocional y social de las personas y comunidades afectadas. El plan, con el que ya se ha llegado a más de 158.000 personas, se está ejecutando en tres fases**:** la primera, ya realizada, derespuesta inmediata**;** una segunda vinculada a larecuperaciónpara la vuelta a la normalidad, y una tercera de fortalecimiento y resilienciapara asegurar que las comunidades y las personas sean más fuertes y estén preparadas ante posibles eventos futuros de emergencias o catástrofes.

Cruz Roja Española continúa su trabajo contra todas las formas de vulnerabilidad, adaptándose y anticipándose a los escenarios de futuro, abierta a la población general, incidiendo en la contribución firme y consistente a los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y la Agenda 2030.

Cruz Roja Española pertenece al Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja, presente en 191 países. Actúa siempre bajo sus siete Principios Fundamentales: Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Carácter Voluntario, Unidad y Universalidad.

reports.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #5: Earthquakes in Venezuela - 28 July 2026
sources: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia
reports.body_text:
As of 28 July, AMDA’s relief team has been working to provide aid to those affected by the earthquakes that devastated Venezuela on 24 June.

AMDA has been based in Caraballeda, La Guaira, one of the hardest-hit locations since the start of the quake response efforts. The below is the summary of its activities between 20-26 July:

■20-23 July

On 20 July, AMDA's relief team treated approximately 50 patients at the temporary clinic in Caraballeda, La Guaira.

Together with local medical volunteers, medical services including blood pressure checks and IV therapy were provided during patient consultations.

The next day, the patient number increased to around 100, while the team underwent staff shuffling. The new team comprised one doctor, two nurses, and a coordinator, who were from Venezuela and Japan.

Nurses on the team were constantly busy with wide range of duties such as taking patients' vital signs, administering IV infusions and inhalation therapy, assisting with electrocardiograms (ECGs), and supporting abdominal ultrasound examinations.

Over the course of two days, the clinic treated patients with a variety of medical needs, including those injured during rescue operations and debris removal, individuals seeking to refill their medication for chronic conditions, and patients suffering from hypertension, joint pain, respiratory illnesses, and other health problems.

Caraballeda became somewhat quieter than before as many of international relief teams had already completed their work and left.

On 22 July, the clinic continued to receive patients with a wide range of medical needs. They included those seeking treatment for chronic conditions such as hypertension, individuals injured while clearing earthquake debris, people suffering from dehydration, and children experiencing fever, insect bites, or parasitic infections. The AMDA team saw around 100 patients that day as well.

On 23 July, the team was joined by a Japanese doctor who arrived from the United States and examined 55 patients in total. In addition to patient consultations, the team provided medicines to those who came to receive medication.

Among those who visited the clinic were people who spoke of losing family members in the earthquake. Recognizing that many survivors required not only physical treatment but also psychological support, the team also referred them to a psychotherapist.

On the same day, H.E. Ambassador Yasushi Sato, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, visited the temporary clinic to observe AMDA's medical activities.

■24-26 July

From 24-26 July, AMDA’s relief team continued providing medical assistance at the temporary clinic in Caraballeda.

Working closely with local healthcare professionals and other partners, the team treated approximately 40 to 90 patients daily. While respiratory symptoms and body aches were commonly observed among patients, mild dehydration (likely caused by fatigue and the intense heat) was also seen.

During the aid work, Venezuelan physicians and medical students working alongside the team shared that they found great fulfillment in being able to provide much-needed medical care at the temporary clinic.

Several also expressed their hope to continue supporting relief efforts in La Guaira even after AMDA concludes its mission.

As 24 July marked precisely one month from the earthquake, all members of the team observed a moment of silence in memory of those affected by the disaster.

Even now, the airport in La Guaira, which had served as the main gateway to the capital, Caracas, remains closed. In surrounding areas, many buildings have either collapsed or are at risk of collapse. It will likely take a considerable amount of time before debris removal is completed.

Some people are still searching for family members who remain missing, while others continue to live in makeshift tents after losing their homes.

The AMDA team will continue to serve the affected communities for the time being.

reports.title: Water Mission Increases Emergency Safe Water Access in Venezuela Through New Strategic Partnerships
reports.body_text:
*Over 18,000 People Served and Nearly 300,000 Liters of Safe Water Produced*

***N. Charleston, S.C. — July 27, 2026** –* [Water Mission](https://link.mediaoutreach.meltwater.com/ls/click?upn=u001.Fjl9RYDvSbHIs4zr2onLy0sBWXb-2FCgIebJ8-2BYVv7WmStxqlsbe82esKsx-2BzRe2rTOkMc_4cIvc4SbN73-2Bn-2F0-2FQmnGing30cPaSgQWcWyrPdP097M6fiBYMJtvCo4itNXjVqVpHweizRZ0tbQg-2FYPuksSOjAf84uuNgmWwnh3nin5AXFY-2BLN61h8TKp6H6DzjMdO2T-2BtljlteY19pEnOszA-2FeGDAH7Wbbodbmlc-2B1kUnr0XcD3W4-2FsxNN0C5qidT0GCzePIp-2FWLtzqZ-2BtBPdeYbo22KFfVaDK9Wa1psYirxLL0f3DlcwbYkx2anNuunmBqaOOn6BEfSdx33O0HTYCjdofDAkBAO75zj95M7YZNVkADE7r4Vj7nlmSlWM1KxpnFSyyzcy-2BstPA4mVGLK8Hl6fQ9ml3ipWbvHEqqE1enF06ORX-2FrjR9VaiHpzxh1F2owwRm-2B), a Christian engineering nonprofit, is scaling their emergency safe water disaster response operations in Venezuela after earthquakes in late June impacted an estimated 6.8 million people with widespread destruction to infrastructure. A month later, Water Mission has installed and is operating water treatment systems at two production locations serving internally displaced people at clinics, schools, churches, and other community sites. These systems are also providing safe, clean water to a robust and growing [mobile water trucking effort](https://link.mediaoutreach.meltwater.com/ls/click?upn=u001.Fjl9RYDvSbHIs4zr2onLyyjhktjJwhbgCrOV05Sa9QiTldWRz-2BzqxRWhfphbY7OtebId5-2Ft8obKN4Hady5I7CA-3D-3Dexhc_4cIvc4SbN73-2Bn-2F0-2FQmnGing30cPaSgQWcWyrPdP097M6fiBYMJtvCo4itNXjVqVpHweizRZ0tbQg-2FYPuksSOjAf84uuNgmWwnh3nin5AXFY-2BLN61h8TKp6H6DzjMdO2T-2BtljlteY19pEnOszA-2FeGDAH7Wbbodbmlc-2B1kUnr0XcD3W4-2FsxNN0C5qidT0GCzePIp-2FWLtzqZ-2BtBPdeYbo22KFfVaDK9Wa1psYirxLL0f3AYvGCngnnxXjRfROFLtkugjJ-2F-2Bi1-2B7CZYqw1i-2BD6Sq6-2FuIK0BKoI46tQvRJrTn8nFQeNeVUDAEruyNOOJNQeBFv0BXcQBaaVeYA5-2FhnauWEtAkbNgllq7PquPcrRAQmboqbPGvQi8ClGmvDdZ9n0Sw) with 21 additional water distribution sites in communities throughout Caraballeda, Catia La Mar, Macuto, and Naiguata.

New and growing strategic global partnerships are aiding this effort and increasing Water Mission’s ability to simultaneously respond to multiple disasters worldwide. [Water Mission was recently welcomed into Integral Alliance,](https://link.mediaoutreach.meltwater.com/ls/click?upn=u001.Fjl9RYDvSbHIs4zr2onLyzW1oXpOUwppL2w-2FfOKnEYPjlB72NlPbvcZLksMe3gOoPPKnOWRIO9UKpaaMqR0vXhvRKzL9-2BfHV0O46xupf9k0bu-2BZARvGXqCDD-2F2UFX47KkeBb0Pp6lHLTDJgHLEfqEA-3D-3D9C6j_4cIvc4SbN73-2Bn-2F0-2FQmnGing30cPaSgQWcWyrPdP097M6fiBYMJtvCo4itNXjVqVpHweizRZ0tbQg-2FYPuksSOjAf84uuNgmWwnh3nin5AXFY-2BLN61h8TKp6H6DzjMdO2T-2BtljlteY19pEnOszA-2FeGDAH7Wbbodbmlc-2B1kUnr0XcD3W4-2FsxNN0C5qidT0GCzePIp-2FWLtzqZ-2BtBPdeYbo22KFfVaDK9Wa1psYirxLL0f3BAeRj4fK9M2SRjD9l4syNVxHRtRYIH7-2FxLmqY8KNZ-2BBvINsKEFiHwm5I9RPcGqDCXuRAf5ipDq-2BdZRgP92yeiF9DarQRwouVKo-2BR-2BMpNWLiK8sWHBv4-2FuFxRy3lT3Z0My9U-2FueHK8nGPmf3DPefFfF) a group of 23 global Christian relief and development organizations with specialized disaster response capabilities. Integral members follow a joint disaster response process when disaster strikes, combining their programming, financial, and communications resources, ensuring a more efficient and rapid response capability that reaches more people in need.

“We are delighted to welcome Water Mission to the Integral family. They bring to the Alliance significant sectoral expertise in water, sanitation, and hygiene, a critical need in both humanitarian situations and long-term international development,” said Carol Bremer-Bennett, Executive Director of World Renew and Chair of the Integral Board. “Water Mission has over 25 years of experience in responding to disasters and already works with some of our members. Their technical expertise will greatly add value to our joint disaster responses, and I am delighted to welcome them to the Integral family.”

[Water Mission is also partnering on a consortium led by Rescue Response International](https://link.mediaoutreach.meltwater.com/ls/click?upn=u001.Fjl9RYDvSbHIs4zr2onLyyjhktjJwhbgCrOV05Sa9QjdiOvdooKdxCmFUENH1HQMsRt8SWVu-2BhkWDhXXCCN2IQ-3D-3DkE9v_4cIvc4SbN73-2Bn-2F0-2FQmnGing30cPaSgQWcWyrPdP097M6fiBYMJtvCo4itNXjVqVpHweizRZ0tbQg-2FYPuksSOjAf84uuNgmWwnh3nin5AXFY-2BLN61h8TKp6H6DzjMdO2T-2BtljlteY19pEnOszA-2FeGDAH7Wbbodbmlc-2B1kUnr0XcD3W4-2FsxNN0C5qidT0GCzePIp-2FWLtzqZ-2BtBPdeYbo22KFfVaDK9Wa1psYirxLL0f3Ayju8Cga9O1Xn85EVgLlzK-2F845n9zonXM7gVCh9NQ5h4axsGQ1mwy3tnjcf-2BQWjBXQG55cQabpELj6UhAGGxw4jqxB2qkjkMIzVoOOX1vVCs1RHXf-2FgHdfKudUYOU1Bu40MRmvz-2FBvXIQ3bDRpQdVa), funded by the U.S. Department of State, to provide disaster response relief in Venezuela in the aftermath of the earthquakes. This partnership, in coordination with generous gifts from Grundfos Foundation, FedEx, Compassion International, Atlas Copco Group, and individual supporters, has enabled Water Mission to provide nearly 300,000 liters of safe water to [over 18,000 people to date](https://link.mediaoutreach.meltwater.com/ls/click?upn=u001.Fjl9RYDvSbHIs4zr2onLyyjhktjJwhbgCrOV05Sa9Qhl-2FrsBUcT5yurBPtQE7NKX3WrcnVrIx37XMWaFvMREUg-3D-3DLdQ5_4cIvc4SbN73-2Bn-2F0-2FQmnGing30cPaSgQWcWyrPdP097M6fiBYMJtvCo4itNXjVqVpHweizRZ0tbQg-2FYPuksSOjAf84uuNgmWwnh3nin5AXFY-2BLN61h8TKp6H6DzjMdO2T-2BtljlteY19pEnOszA-2FeGDAH7Wbbodbmlc-2B1kUnr0XcD3W4-2FsxNN0C5qidT0GCzePIp-2FWLtzqZ-2BtBPdeYbo22KFfVaDK9Wa1psYirxLL0f3DpQktYl1ALgFWbS93kUg0FmapthqFa1s-2BeRUm1zT-2FuBQhbrdTwM7ZjG3445vGtwnrgIIBm6ZFWbdY4rJ8S4y-2FLytx6Zb2v2cPRXEFuwpRYJKphB01-2BOEcfFA92IboSmFqJTw3cEe-2BCtjKYcnyttsTr). Safe, clean drinking water is critical during any disaster, helping to prevent the spread of waterborne illnesses, which are particularly deadly for children.

“In the aftermath of a disaster, access to safe water is one of the most urgent needs and every day matters,” said Water Mission CEO and President George C. Greene IV, PE. “What we are seeing in Venezuela demonstrates the power of strong partnerships combined with proven technical expertise. By working alongside organizations committed to serving people in crisis, we have been able to move quickly, establish safe water production, and expand distribution to reach thousands of people. We are grateful for every partner and supporter helping us bring safe water and hope to people during this critical time.”

Water Mission has responded to nearly 90 disasters worldwide over the past 25 years, bringing an extensive background in providing immediate and long-term safe water solutions. The organization has served more than 8 million people globally since 2001. To learn more or to support their ongoing disaster response efforts in Venezuela, please visit [https://watermission.org/venezuela-earthquake-response](https://watermission.org/venezuela-earthquake-response).

**About Water Mission**  
 Water Mission is a Christian engineering nonprofit that builds sustainable safe water solutions for people in developing countries, refugee camps, and disaster areas. Since 2001, Water Mission has served more than 8 million people in more than 65 countries, sharing safe water and the message of God’s love. Water Mission’s global headquarters is in North Charleston, SC, and the organization serves people in Africa; Asia; and North, South, and Central America. reports.body_html:
Over 18,000 People Served and Nearly 300,000 Liters of Safe Water Produced

N. Charleston, S.C. — July 27, 2026 – Water Mission, a Christian engineering nonprofit, is scaling their emergency safe water disaster response operations in Venezuela after earthquakes in late June impacted an estimated 6.8 million people with widespread destruction to infrastructure. A month later, Water Mission has installed and is operating water treatment systems at two production locations serving internally displaced people at clinics, schools, churches, and other community sites. These systems are also providing safe, clean water to a robust and growing mobile water trucking effort with 21 additional water distribution sites in communities throughout Caraballeda, Catia La Mar, Macuto, and Naiguata.

New and growing strategic global partnerships are aiding this effort and increasing Water Mission’s ability to simultaneously respond to multiple disasters worldwide. Water Mission was recently welcomed into Integral Alliance, a group of 23 global Christian relief and development organizations with specialized disaster response capabilities. Integral members follow a joint disaster response process when disaster strikes, combining their programming, financial, and communications resources, ensuring a more efficient and rapid response capability that reaches more people in need.

“We are delighted to welcome Water Mission to the Integral family. They bring to the Alliance significant sectoral expertise in water, sanitation, and hygiene, a critical need in both humanitarian situations and long-term international development,” said Carol Bremer-Bennett, Executive Director of World Renew and Chair of the Integral Board. “Water Mission has over 25 years of experience in responding to disasters and already works with some of our members. Their technical expertise will greatly add value to our joint disaster responses, and I am delighted to welcome them to the Integral family.”

Water Mission is also partnering on a consortium led by Rescue Response International, funded by the U.S. Department of State, to provide disaster response relief in Venezuela in the aftermath of the earthquakes. This partnership, in coordination with generous gifts from Grundfos Foundation, FedEx, Compassion International, Atlas Copco Group, and individual supporters, has enabled Water Mission to provide nearly 300,000 liters of safe water to over 18,000 people to date. Safe, clean drinking water is critical during any disaster, helping to prevent the spread of waterborne illnesses, which are particularly deadly for children.

“In the aftermath of a disaster, access to safe water is one of the most urgent needs and every day matters,” said Water Mission CEO and President George C. Greene IV, PE. “What we are seeing in Venezuela demonstrates the power of strong partnerships combined with proven technical expertise. By working alongside organizations committed to serving people in crisis, we have been able to move quickly, establish safe water production, and expand distribution to reach thousands of people. We are grateful for every partner and supporter helping us bring safe water and hope to people during this critical time.”

Water Mission has responded to nearly 90 disasters worldwide over the past 25 years, bringing an extensive background in providing immediate and long-term safe water solutions. The organization has served more than 8 million people globally since 2001. To learn more or to support their ongoing disaster response efforts in Venezuela, please visit https://watermission.org/venezuela-earthquake-response.

About Water Mission
Water Mission is a Christian engineering nonprofit that builds sustainable safe water solutions for people in developing countries, refugee camps, and disaster areas. Since 2001, Water Mission has served more than 8 million people in more than 65 countries, sharing safe water and the message of God’s love. Water Mission’s global headquarters is in North Charleston, SC, and the organization serves people in Africa; Asia; and North, South, and Central America. Charity Navigator has awarded Water Mission its top four-star rating 19 years in a row, a distinction shared by less than 1% of the charities rated by the organization. To learn more, visit watermission.org, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, or X.

reports.title: UNICEF Venezuela Humanitarian Situation Report No.6 (Earthquake Response), 21–24 July 2026
reports.body_text:
**Highlights**

- One month after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela’s north-central coast, children and families continue to face the lasting impacts of displacement, damaged infrastructure and disruption to essential services.
- UNICEF has provided hygiene supplies to 8,906 people and integrated WASH services to 3,237 people; enabled 21,000 people to access primary health care, including 16,006 people vaccinated; and reached 5,282 children and women with nutrition services. UNICEF also supported more than 4,000 children, adolescents and caregivers with child protection services, including 205 referrals for specialized care, while strengthening education support.
- Through an integrated humanitarian response, UNICEF aims to reach 470,000 people, including 169,000 children, with life-saving assistance and early recovery support. In addition to its US$137.6 million HAC appeal, UNICEF requires an additional US$65.7 million to sustain critical interventions and support the implementation of the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan Addendum.

reports.body_text:
*This Situation Report provides an overview of the twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026 (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5), and their impact on telecommunications. It outlines the activities of the WFP-led Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC)1 Telecoms Area in supporting emergency communications for the humanitarian response. The Cluster is currently not formally activated for this emergency.*

**Summary Points**

• LTC Telecoms in Venezuela is working with government authorities, mobile network operators, internet service providers (ISPs), the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), and other partners to restore critical communications, and prioritize support in the most affected areas.

• LTC Telecoms is strengthening power continuity across response sites through real-time monitoring of battery systems linked to solar-powered internet connectivity. This provides timely visibility on energy gaps, allowing teams to monitor and take corrective action to keep critical internet connectivity services operational for over 1,400 humanitarian responders and affected communities.

• Grupo Telefónica has provided a charging kiosk at each of Polideportivo and César Nieves, supporting 48 power-strip connections, enabling affected people to charge mobile phones and other Information Communication Technology (ICT) devices to maintain access to communication, information and basic services. The kiosks will be returned to Grupo Telefónica once the emergency transitions fully into recovery.

reports.body_text:
El decimosexto Reporte de Situación presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela, con información correspondiente al período del 22 al 23 de julio.

## **Aspectos destacados**

Entre el 22 y el 23 de julio, la OIM continuó su respuesta multisectorial en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas mediante intervenciones en alojamiento y coordinación de sitios, salud, protección, WASH y gestión de información.

A la fecha, la OIM ha alcanzado a **8.676 personas únicas mediante 16.265 asistencias y servicios**, principalmente en alojamiento y coordinación de campamentos transitorios, salud, WASH y protección.

La OIM y su socio Fundación Vivienda Popular han distribuido **3.175 sets de cocina, 3.617 lonas, 2.115 baldes, 1.759 lámparas solares y 819 kits de refugio** a hogares afectados.

## **Actividades de la OIM**

La OIM continuó gestionando y coordinando cinco campamentos transitorios en La Guaira y avanzó la transición operativa de tres de ellos al Consejo Noruego para los Refugiados (NRC).

En el Campo de Golf de Tanaguarena continuó la organización de espacios para alojamiento y prestación de servicios, mientras que en Mare Abajo II se actualizó la capacidad de alojamiento y continuó el seguimiento a la posible reubicación de familias desde Playa Grande.

En WASH, continuó ampliando el acceso a artículos para almacenamiento seguro de agua e higiene. A la fecha, se han distribuido **1.552 bidones plegables, 1.091 kits de higiene y 93 bidones**.

La OIM y su socio Ven Da Tu Mano han realizado **6.194 asistencias y servicios de salud**, incluyendo atención primaria, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial. Los servicios móviles de salud y SMAPS continuaron operativos en el Polideportivo José María Vargas y el Estadio César Nieves.

La OIM finalizó la Encuesta de Hogares en Campamentos Transitorios y el análisis de flujos de movilidad durante los primeros 15 días de julio, al tiempo que avanzó la preparación de una evaluación de los 107 campamentos transitorios.

En protección, continuó brindando orientación, asistencia legal, apoyo en documentación y derivaciones a servicios especializados, con **218 asistencias y servicios de protección registrados a la fecha**, mientras que 130 personas han recibido atención y acompañamiento especializado.

## **Respuesta planificada de la OIM**

La OIM continuará la transición operativa de tres campamentos a NRC, las mejoras de infraestructura y prestación de servicios, y reforzará los servicios de WASH, salud, salud mental y protección.

Asimismo, fortalecerá el monitoreo de los campamentos y de la movilidad, avanzará las evaluaciones de campamentos transitorios y poblaciones afectadas, y continuará la coordinación con autoridades y socios humanitarios.

reports.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #16 (22 to 23 July 2026)
reports.body_text:
The sixteenth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, covering the period from 22 to 23 July.

## **Highlights**

Between 22 and 23 July, IOM continued its multisectoral response in transitory camps and affected communities through interventions in shelter and site coordination, health, protection, WASH and information management.

To date, IOM has reached **8,676 unique individuals through 16,265 instances of assistance and services**, mainly in shelter and transitory camp coordination, health, WASH and protection.

IOM and its partner Fundación Vivienda Popular have distributed **3,175 kitchen sets, 3,617 tarpaulins, 2,115 buckets, 1,759 solar lamps and 819 shelter kits** to affected households.

## **IOM activities**

IOM continued managing and coordinating five transitory camps in La Guaira and advanced the operational transition of three of them to the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC).

At Tanaguarena Golf Course, IOM continued preparations to expand accommodation and service provision capacity, while in Mare Abajo II accommodation capacity was updated with 206 bunk beds and 635 mattresses recorded.

In WASH, IOM continued expanding access to safe water storage and hygiene items. To date, **1,552 collapsible water containers, 1,091 hygiene kits and 93 water containers** have been distributed.

IOM and its partner Ven Da Tu Mano have provided **6,194 health assistance and services**, including primary healthcare, mental health and psychosocial support. Mobile health and MHPSS teams remained operational at José María Vargas Sports Complex and César Nieves Stadium.

IOM finalized the Household Survey in Transitory Camps and the analysis of mobility flows during the first 15 days of July, while advancing preparations for the assessment of 107 transitory camps.

In protection, IOM continued providing guidance, legal assistance, documentation support and referrals to specialized services, with **218 protection assistance and services recorded to date**.

## **IOM planned response**

IOM will continue the operational transition of three camps to NRC, infrastructure improvements and service delivery activities, while strengthening WASH, health, mental health and protection services.

It will also strengthen camp and mobility monitoring, advance assessments of transitory camps and affected populations, and continue coordination with authorities and humanitarian partners.

reports.title: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 24 de julio 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**CIFRAS CLAVE**

- 5,3K personas fallecidas tras dos poderosos terremotos que sacudieron Venezuela el 24 de junio
- 43,5K casos confirmados de sarampión en América Latina y el Caribe en 2026, 3,8 veces más que en 2025
- 61K personas quedaron aisladas debido a fuertes tormentas en Chile

**VENEZUELA: TERREMOTO**

Un mes después de los terremotos del 24 de junio que sacudieron el centro-norte de Venezuela, los socios humanitarios continúan ampliando la asistencia en las zonas más afectadas, mientras las autoridades avanzan en los esfuerzos de recuperación y reconstrucción para las comunidades afectadas. Al 22 de julio, el número de personas fallecidas ha aumentado a 5.398 y las autoridades han registrado más de 1.460 réplicas. Unas 23.843 personas permanecen en 107 campamentos transitorios. Los socios humanitarios están brindando asistencia en materia de salud, alimentación, protección, alojamiento y WASH en los estados más afectados. Más de 117.000 personas han tenido acceso a servicios esenciales y apoyo humanitario a través de la respuesta coordinada. La planificación de recuperación y reconstrucción también avanza, incluyendo esfuerzos para identificar soluciones de vivienda para las familias afectadas. Persisten necesidades significativas en materia de alojamiento, servicios básicos, seguridad alimentaria y apoyo psicosocial.

[Apoya aquí al Fondo Humanitario Venezolano](https://crisisrelief.un.org/en/donate-venezuela-crisis)

Para más información, visita: [ReliefWeb Response](https://response.reliefweb.int/es/venezuela/terremoto-junio-2026)

**CHILE: FUERTES LLUVIAS**

Las autoridades han declarado estado de catástrofe en la región chilena de Coquimbo, la provincia de Huasco y en la comuna de Tierra Amarilla, provincia de Copiapó, debido a un sistema de tormentas que comenzó el 13 de julio en 11 de las 16 regiones del país. Al 22 de julio, el Servicio Nacional de Prevención y Respuesta ante Desastres (SENAPRED) informa que el clima severo ha afectado a 3.532 personas, dejando 13 personas fallecidas y 4 personas aún desaparecidas. Las precipitaciones han alcanzado niveles históricos de hasta 200 mm en algunas zonas. Más de 1.500 personas permanecen en albergues, concentrados en las regiones de Valparaíso, La Araucanía, Biobío y Coquimbo. El sismo, cuyo epicentro se ubicó cerca de la provincia de Chupaca, a unos 300 km al este de Lima, provocó una réplica de magnitud 3,7 y derrumbó decenas de viviendas en un distrito rural poco poblado, con menos de 5.000 habitantes, dejando a cientos de personas desplazadas. Dos hospitales y varias estructuras históricas sufrieron daños y se reportaron cortes de electricidad en las comunidades afectadas. El Gobierno ha desplegado alrededor de 100 profesionales de la salud y un hospital móvil, mientras que los bomberos y el personal de las fuerzas armadas continúan limpiando escombros y buscando a quienes aún puedan estar atrapados. Las autoridades advirtieron que las cifras de víctimas podrían aumentar a medida que continúen las evaluaciones en comunidades más remotas.

**REGIONAL: SARAMPIÓN**

El sarampión sigue siendo una preocupación de salud pública en las América, aunque las tendencias de transmisión se han ralentizado en las últimas semanas. Entre las semanas epidemiológicas 1 y 27 de 2026, las autoridades informan de 43.559 casos confirmados y 44 muertes en 17 países y territorios, lo que representa un aumento de 3,8 veces respecto al mismo periodo de 2025. Durante las dos últimas semanas de reporte, se notificaron 1.818 nuevos casos, lo que representa una disminución del 38% respecto al periodo anterior. Guatemala, México, Estados Unidos y Canadá representan el 98% de todos los casos notificados en la región. Tras los recientes terremotos en Venezuela, los socios de salud continúan priorizando las actividades de vigilancia y vacunación para reducir el riesgo de transmisión del sarampión entre las poblaciones desplazadas que viven en alojamientos temporales.

reports.title: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 24 July 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**KEY FIGURES**

- 5.3K people dead after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela on 24 June
- 43.5K confirmed cases of measles in LAC in 2026, 3.8 times higher than 2025
- 61K people isolated due to severe storms in Chile

**VENEZUELA: EARTHQUAKE**

One month after the 24 June earthquakes that struck north-central Venezuela, humanitarian partners continue to scale up assistance across the most affected areas, while authorities advance recovery and reconstruction efforts for impacted communities. As of 22 July, the death toll has risen to 5,398 and authorities have recorded more than 1,460 aftershocks. Some 23,843 people remain in 107 transitional camps. Humanitarian partners are providing health, food, protection, shelter and WASH assistance across the most affected states. More than 117,000 people have now accessed essential services and humanitarian support through the coordinated response. Recovery and reconstruction planning is also advancing, including efforts to identify housing solutions for affected families. Significant needs persist in shelter, basic services, food security and psychosocial support.

[Support the Venezuelan Humanitarian Fund here](https://crisisrelief.un.org/en/donate-venezuela-crisis)

For more information, visit: [ReliefWeb Response](https://response.reliefweb.int/es/venezuela/terremoto-junio-2026)

**CHILE: HEAVY RAINFALL**

Authorities have declared a state of catastrophe in Chile’s Coquimbo region, Huasco province and in the Tierra Amarilla commune, Copiapó province, due to a storm system that began on 13 July across 11 of the country’s 16 regions. As of 22 July, the National Disaster Prevention and Response Service (SENAPRED) report that the severe weather has affected 3,532 people, left 13 dead and 4 still missing. Rainfall has reached historic levels of up to 200mm in some areas. More than 1,500 people remain in shelters, concentrated in the Valparaíso, La Araucanía, Biobío, and Coquimbo regions. Although access has been restored in some areas, at least 61,000 people remain cut off. The Chilean Red Cross has activated a yellow alert and is coordinating with SENAPRED.

**PERU: EARTHQUAKE**

A magnitude 5.1 earthquake about 10 km deep struck the Junín region of central Peru on 18 July, killing at least six people and injuring more than 30, according to Peru’s National Institute of Civil Defense (INDECI). The quake, centered near Chupaca province roughly 300 km east of Lima, triggered a magnitude 3.7 aftershock and collapsed dozens of homes in a sparsely populated rural district of fewer than 5,000 people, leaving hundreds displaced. Two hospitals and several historic structures sustained damage, and power outages were reported in affected communities. The Government has deployed around 100 health professionals and a mobile hospital, while firefighters and armed forces personnel continue clearing debris and searching for anyone still trapped. Authorities cautioned that casualty figures could rise as assessments in more remote communities continue.

**REGIONAL: MEASLES**

Measles remains a public health concern across the Americas, although transmission trends have slowed in recent weeks. Between epidemiological weeks 1 and 27 of 2026, authorities report 43,559 confirmed cases and 44 deaths across 17 countries and territories, representing a 3.8-fold increase compared with the same period in 2025. During the last two reporting weeks, 1,818 new cases were reported, representing a 38 per cent decrease compared with the previous reporting period. Guatemala, Mexico, the United States and Canada account for 98 per cent of all reported cases in the region. Following the recent earthquakes in Venezuela, health partners continue to prioritize surveillance and vaccination activities to reduce the risk of measles transmission among displaced populations living in temporary shelters.
