reports.title: Venezuela Earthquakes Situation Report #3 (July 13, 2026)
reports.body_text:
**FAST FACTS**

- On June 24, two earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 hit northern Venezuela consecutively, impacting at least seven states—including the capital city of Caracas and the neighboring city of La Guaira. In response, the government declared a state of emergency.
- A reported 9.73 million people have been affected by the quakes, with more than 530,000 people having been exposed to extreme earthquake intensity.
- Official figures have confirmed more than 4,490 fatalities, 16,700 injuries, 6,400 people rescued and nearly 18,000 without housing.
- Affected populations have been left without access to basic necessities such as medicines, healthcare services, food and safe water.

**OUR RESPONSE**

- International Medical Corps’ rapid-response teams immediately deployed after the quakes, conducting a rapid needs assessment on June 25.
- Based on identified needs, International Medical Corps deployed an mobile medical unit (MMU) that has so far provided 1,273 consultations since beginning operations.
- On July 11, International Medical Corps opened an Emergency Medical Team (EMT) Type 1 Fixed facility to provide free medical services to impacted communities.
- Our teams have so far provided 164 consultations through the EMT Type 1 Fixed facility.
- International Medical Corps has conducted a detailed assessment of shelters housing displaced persons, and is conducting water trucking to multiple affected camps.

Needs are continuing to increase given the compromised living conditions and increased risk of communicable disease, accumulation of waste in affected communities, and the upcoming rainy season and associated flooding. As the situation on the ground evolves, International Medical Corps is continuing to communicate with local and international organizations involved in the response, to ensure that we continue to provide critically needed services in an effective, coordinated manner.

reports.title: WFP Venezuela Earthquakes Response Situation Report #5 - 12 July 2026
reports.body_text:
Funding  
USD 80 Million required to support families affected by the earthquakes.  
USD 20 Million for regular programmes, including school feeding. Resources and stock from regular programmes have been redirected to the emergency, making donor support critical on both fronts. Situation

Update  
• After the twin earthquakes of 24 June, families in the most affected areas continue to face dire conditions, depending on humanitarian assistance as a critical lifeline. Official figures now report over 4,490 deaths, with the toll still expected to rise.  
• WFP data collection across the seven most affected states reveals damage to infrastructure, disruptions to basic services, and severe impacts on livelihoods. Households struggle to access food and essential items, consistently identifying food assistance, safe drinking water, healthcare, and medicines, and hygiene items as their most urgent needs.  
• Commercial activity is gradually recovering, though significant challenges remain, including rising prices, transport constraints, and shortages of essential goods. In specific communities, however, markets are now functioning well enough to reliably supply food to families with purchasing capacity.

reports.title: Cáritas Española aumenta a un millón los fondos para responder a la emergencia humanitaria causada por el doble terremoto en Venezuela
reports.body_text:
**• Se une al equipo que gestiona la atención a la urgencia bajo el liderazgo de Cáritas Venezuela**

**• En las primeras semanas, la campaña “Cáritas con Venezuela” alcanza los 5 millones de euros**

Cáritas.- 13 de julio de 2026. Ante la crisis humanitaria causada por el doble terremoto del pasado 24 de junio en el norte de Venezuela, Cáritas Española ha decidido aumentar a un millón de euros los fondos que se enviarán a Cáritas Venezuela para responder a las necesidades de las personas afectadas por esta catástrofe. Esta partida incluye los 300.000 euros que ya han sido movilizados durante los primeros días de la tragedia. Además, ha desplazado a un cooperante con base en Bogotá (Colombia), que ya se ha incorporado al equipo de Cáritas Venezuela para apoyar en la coordinación de la respuesta y su operativa.

reports.title: Dispatch of the Second Japan Disaster Relief Medical Team in Response to the Earthquake Damage in Venezuela
reports.body_text:
In light of the high demand for medical support in the earthquake-affected areas of Venezuela, the Government of Japan decided to dispatch the second batch of the Japan Disaster Relief (JDR) Medical Team to the affected area. The second team consists of staff of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), as well as registered doctors, nurses, and other health professionals, and is scheduled to depart Japan for Venezuela next week.  
  
The Government of Japan will continue to stand by the people of Venezuela and provide necessary assistance based on local needs.

## (Reference) Overview of Damage

In Venezuela, a magnitude 7+ earthquake that occurred at approximately 7:00 a.m. Japan Standard Time on Thursday, June 25, caused numerous casualties, including deaths and injuries, and property damage. According to the Venezuelan government's announcement, the damage includes 3,889 deaths and over 16,740 injuries (as of July 10, 6:00a.m.). According to an assessment by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), approximately 58,870 buildings across the affected areas may have been destroyed or damaged. The full extent of the damage is still unknown.

reports.title: Emergency Grant and Other Humanitarian Assistance in Response to the Earthquake Disaster in Venezuela
reports.body_text:
On July 10, the Government of Japan decided to provide an Emergency Grant of USD 3.5 million in response to the earthquake disaster in Venezuela.

With this Emergency Grant, the Government of Japan will provide humanitarian assistance in key sectors, including food, health and medical care, shelters and non-food items through the World Food Programme (WFP), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

1. In response to the earthquake disaster in Venezuela, the Government of Japan had already decided on June 30 to provide emergency relief goods, such as plastic sheet (Tarpaulin), portable jerry can, and water purifier, through the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), and on July 1 to dispatch the Japan Disaster Relief Medical Team. In addition, Japan Platform (JPF), a mechanism for emergency humanitarian assistance by NGOs, the business community and the government, plans to implement approximately USD 1 million of humanitarian assistance funded by the Japanese government’s grant.
2. The Government of Japan intends to work closely with relevant agencies and organizations to provide the necessary assistance that benefits the people of Venezuela in a timely manner.

## (Reference1) Implementing agencies, areas of assistance, and the amount of disbursement:

- - WFP: Food \[USD 1.5 million\]
- - IFRC: Health and medical care \[USD 1 million\]
- - IOM: Shelter and non-food items \[USD 1 million\]

## (Reference2) Overview of Damage (as of July 10, 6 a.m.)

In Venezuela, an earthquake measuring more than magnitude 7.0 that occurred at approximately 7:00 a.m. Japan Standard Time on Thursday, June 25, caused numerous casualties, and extensive property damage. According to the Venezuelan government's announcement, the damage includes 3,889 deaths and over 16,740 injuries. According to an assessment by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), approximately 58,870 buildings across the affected areas may have been destroyed or damaged. The full extent of the damage is still unknown.

## (Reference3) Humanitarian assistance through JPF

The amount of contributions: JPY 150 million (Approximately USD 1 million) Based on the ongoing needs assessment in the field, JPF member NGOs will provide support to disaster victims, utilizing funds provided by the Japanese government to JPF.

reports.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #19 (12 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**Situation Report No. 19**  
**Earthquakes in Venezuela**  
**12 July 2026**  
**Time: 9:00 pm**

**Highlights**

- Following the 24 June earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 (18:00 local time), **authorities report more than 1,200 aftershocks.**
- Official toll: **4,490 people dead and 16,740 injured.**
- A total of **6,462 people have been rescued.**
- **Tom Fletcher, the United Nations humanitarian chief, concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP).**
- **An additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response and address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.**
- The United Nations system and its partner organizations, in coordination with the Government, are responding with multisectoral actions and will continue to scale up assistance to affected people.

**Situation overview**

Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive high-magnitude earthquakes (7.2 and 7.5) that struck on 24 June (18:00 local time) in the north-central region, with the epicentre located along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Authorities report 1,222 aftershocks.**

Eighteen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of **4,490 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency**. Authorities also indicated that **17,907 people remain without housing**. According to official reports of 11 July, 315 of those who died have yet to be identified.

The Government response remains focused on search operations, the management of transitional camps and assistance to affected populations. The United Nations and its partner organizations, in coordination with the authorities, continue implementing multisectoral response activities and scaling up assistance. United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher concluded his visit to Venezuela this week and called on the international community to sustain support for the humanitarian response. In this context, he **announced a US$298 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan, aimed at addressing the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months**.

Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos

 transitorios y la atención de las personas afectadas. Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en articulación con las autoridades, realizan acciones multisectoriales para las personas afectadas y continuarán ampliando la respuesta. En ese contexto, anunció una adenda al Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria por 298 millones de dólares, destinada a atender las necesidades multisectoriales de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.

reports.title: Situation Report No.5: Earthquakes in Venezuela 2026 (M7.2 and M7.5), 12 July 2026
reports.body_text:
**HIGHLIGHTS**

- On 24 June 2026, two consecutive earthquakes (M7.2 and M7.5) struck north-central Venezuela, affecting at least seven states, with La Guaira the most severely impacted. Authorities have since reported more than 1,202 aftershocks.
- **The health response has transitioned from rapid damage assessments to restoring the continuity of essential health services**. Functional constraints persist across the affected health network, particularly in La Guaira, where reduced hospital capacity continues to limit specialized care and increase pressure on referral pathways.
- Recovery efforts are focused on restoring health system functionality through coordinated assessments, health facility recovery and Emergency Medical Team (EMT) support. **Damage has been identified in 38 health facilities** across the three most affected states, while Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) remains a priority need, particularly in La Guaira and temporary shelters**.**
- PAHO/WHO is actively supporting the Ministry of Health (MPPS) in deployed **seven Regional Response Team specialists** covering health emergency coordination, logistics, information systems and media, epidemiology, risk communication and community engagement, EMT coordination, and rapid health facility assessment. In coordination with MoH, PAHO/WHO is supporting the **virtual CICOM and EMT mobilization: Thirteen EMTs are operational in La Guaira, Caracas and Miranda and Aragua** increasing clinical capacity in affected areas.
- PAHO/WHO has **locally distributed** an initial 6 tons of supplies, delivering Trauma and Emergency Surgery Kits **to 4 high-complexity hospitals** and medication and equipment modules to **5 community health areas (ASIC) and a specialized clinic**. A chartered plane (with ~27.5 metric tons of supplies) is now being coordinated, carrying Interagency Emergency Health Kits, additional surgery kits, and Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) treatment kits to further strengthen referral hospitals and primary care networks.

In coordination with MoH, PAHO/WHO is supporting the virtual CICOM and EMT mobilization: Thirteen EMTs are operational in La Guaira, Caracas and Miranda and Aragua increasing clinical capacity in affected areas.
  • PAHO/WHO has locally distributed an initial 6 tons of supplies, delivering Trauma and Emergency Surgery Kits to 4 high-complexity hospitals and medication and equipment modules to 5 community health areas (ASIC) and a specialized clinic. A chartered plane (with ~27.5 metric tons of supplies) is now being coordinated, carrying Interagency Emergency Health Kits, additional surgery kits, and Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) treatment kits to further strengthen referral hospitals and primary care networks.

reports.body_text:
**Situation Report No. 18**  
**Earthquakes in Venezuela**  
**11 July 2026**  
**Time: 9:00 pm**

**Highlights**

- Following the 24 June earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 (18:00 local time), **authorities report more than 1,170 aftershocks.**
- Official toll: **4,333 people dead and 16,740 injured.**
- A total of **6,462 people have been rescued.**
- **Tom Fletcher, the United Nations humanitarian chief, concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP).**
- **An additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response and address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.**
- The United Nations system and its partner organizations, in coordination with the Government, are responding with multisectoral actions and will continue to scale up assistance to affected people.

Situation overview

Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive high-magnitude earthquakes (7.2 and 7.5) that struck on 24 June (18:00 local time) in the north-central region, with the epicentre located along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Authorities report 1,171 aftershocks.**

Seventeen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of **4,333 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency.** Authorities also indicated that **17,907 people remain without housing.** According to official reports, 315 of those who died have yet to be identified, while search operations for possible survivors remain active at priority sites.

The Government response remains focused on search operations, the management of transitional camps and assistance to affected populations. The United Nations and its partner organizations, in coordination with the authorities, continue implementing multisectoral response activities and scaling up assistance. United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher concluded his visit to Venezuela this week and called on the international community to sustain support for the humanitarian response. In this context, he **announced a US$298 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan, aimed at addressing the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.**

reports.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #18 (11 de julio de 2026, Hora: 09:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**Reporte de situación N.º 18**  
**Terremotos en Venezuela**  
**11 de julio de 2026**  
**Hora: 9:00 pm**

**Destacados**

- Tras los sismos de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5 del 24 de junio (18:00 hora local), **las autoridades reportan más de 1.170 réplicas.**
- Balance oficial: **4.333 personas fallecidas y 16.740 heridas.**
- **6.462 personas han sido rescatadas.**
- **Tom Fletcher, jefe humanitario de las Naciones Unidas, concluyó su visita de cuatro días al país e hizo un llamado a mantener el compromiso internacional con el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria.**
- **Se lanzó un llamamiento adicional por US$298 millones para ampliar la respuesta a los terremotos y atender las necesidades de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.**
- El Sistema de Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en coordinación con el gobierno, responden con acciones multisectoriales y continuarán ampliando la asistencia a las personas afectadas.

**Situación general**

Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos el 24 de junio (18:00, hora local) en la región centro-norte, con epicentro sobre el eje San Felipe - Yumare - Montalbán (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Las autoridades reportan 1.171 réplicas.**

A 17 días de los terremotos, las autoridades reportan un balance de **4.333 personas fallecidas, 16.740 personas heridas y 6.462 personas rescatadas desde el inicio de la emergencia.** Asimismo, indicaron que **17.907 personas permanecen sin vivienda.** Según las autoridades, 315 de las personas fallecidas continúan sin ser identificadas y las labores de búsqueda de sobrevivientes permanecen activas en sitios priorizados.

La respuesta gubernamental mantiene el foco en las labores de búsqueda, la gestión de los campamentos transitorios y la atención de las personas afectadas. Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en articulación con las autoridades, realizan acciones multisectoriales para las personas afectadas y continuarán ampliando la respuesta. El Subsecretario General de las Naciones Unidas para Asuntos Humanitarios y Coordinador del Socorro de Emergencia, Tom Fletcher, concluyó esta semana su visita a Venezuela e instó a la comunidad internacional a mantener el apoyo a la respuesta humanitaria. En ese contexto, **anunció una adenda al Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria por 298 millones de dólares, destinada a atender las necesidades multisectoriales de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.**

reports.title: Terremotos Venezuela: Adenda al Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria 2026 [EN/ES]
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
(English below)

Los terremotos de magnitud **7,2** y **7,5** que sacudieron el centro-norte de Venezuela el 24 de junio de 2026 provocaron una destrucción generalizada de viviendas, infraestructura pública, establecimientos de salud, escuelas y servicios esenciales en siete estados del país: La Guaira, Distrito Capital, Miranda, Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón y Yaracuy. Según datos oficiales del 11 de julio, más de 4.000 personas fallecieron, cerca de 17.000 resultaron heridas y 17.900 quedaron sin vivienda. Más de 18.000 personas permanecen en campamentos temporales o en alojamientos precarios, mientras las comunidades afectadas enfrentan interrupciones de servicios básicos, pérdida de medios de vida y condiciones de vida cada vez más frágiles.

El terremoto agravó las necesidades de una población que ya enfrentaba importantes desafíos en el acceso a servicios básicos y oportunidades económicas. Los daños a viviendas e infraestructura crítica han aumentado la presión sobre los sistemas de salud, agua, saneamiento, educación y protección, al tiempo que han reducido la capacidad de recuperación de los hogares afectados. La Evaluación Rápida de Necesidades, complementada con el análisis de información secundaria, la evaluación de modelos estadísticos e imágenes satelitales, junto con la valoración de especialistas confirman un deterioro multisectorial de las condiciones de vida y señalan necesidades urgentes en salud, agua segura, seguridad alimentaria, protección, alojamiento y apoyo psicosocial. Paralelamente, actores nacionales e internacionales han ampliado las operaciones de respuesta para proporcionar asistencia vital y apoyar los esfuerzos liderados por las autoridades.

Esta adenda al Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria (PRH) 2026 presenta la estrategia del Equipo Humanitario de País para responder al impacto de los terremotos durante un período de seis meses. El plan busca asistir a **1,3 millones** de personas afectadas y requiere **US$299 millones** adicionales para complementar las actividades ya contempladas en el PRH 2026. Con ello, los requerimientos financieros totales del plan aumentan de US$632 millones a **US$931 millones** y la población objetivo total se amplía de 5,5 millones a **6,2 millones** de personas. Las cifras presentadas podrán ajustarse a medida que evolucione la situación y se disponga de nueva información sobre las necesidades y la respuesta.

\-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 on the Richter scale, which struck north-central Venezuela on 24 June 2026, caused widespread destruction to homes, public infrastructure, healthcare facilities, schools and essential services in seven states across the country: La Guaira, the Capital District, Miranda, Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón and Yaracuy. According to official figures as of 11 July, more than 4,000 people died, nearly 17,000 were injured, and 17,900 were left homeless. More than 18,000 people remain in temporary camps or makeshift accommodation, whilst affected communities face disruptions to basic services, loss of livelihoods and increasingly precarious living conditions.

The earthquake has exacerbated the needs of a population that was already facing significant challenges in accessing basic services and economic opportunities. Damage to homes and critical infrastructure has increased pressure on health, water, sanitation, education and protection systems, whilst reducing the resilience of affected households. A Rapid Needs Assessment (RNA), supplemented by an analysis of secondary data, an evaluation of statistical models and satellite imagery, as well as expert assessments, confirms a multi-sectoral deterioration in living conditions and highlights urgent needs in health, safe water, food security, protection, shelter, and psychosocial support. At the same time, national and international actors have scaled up response operations to provide vital assistance and support the efforts led by the authorities.

This addendum to the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) sets out the Humanitarian Country Team’s strategy for responding to the impact of the earthquakes over a six-month period. The plan aims to assist **1.3 million** people and requires an additional **US$299 million** to supplement the activities already included in the 2026 HRP. As a result, the plan’s total funding requirements rise from $632 million to **$931 million**, and the total target population increases from 5.5 million to **6.2 million** people. These figures may be adjusted as the situation evolves and new information on needs and response becomes available.

Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #10 (9 July 2026)
reports.body_text:
The tenth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela as of 9 July. It also includes the priorities of IOM’s Funding Appeal to scale up urgent assistance.

**Highlights**

In La Guaira, IOM and its partners strengthened assistance in transitory camps. At César Nieves Stadium, they continued improving spaces and distributed tarpaulins and kitchen sets, while at José María Vargas Sports Centre, services were expanded to include dental and psychiatric care, reaching 290 health and mental health consultations.

To date, IOM has reached 4,526 unique individuals through 7,273 assistance and distribution services, mainly in health, shelter and site coordination, and protection.

IOM maintains its USD 98 million Funding Appeal to assist 850,000 people and support 140 entities between July and December 2026.

**IOM Activities**

IOM continues supporting prioritized transitory camps in La Guaira, including César Nieves Stadium, José María Vargas Sports Centre and Playa Grande, through site coordination, shelter, registration, WASH, health and mental health, protection and information management.

At César Nieves Stadium, 341 tarpaulins and 334 kitchen sets were distributed. To date, 830 tarpaulins and 825 kitchen sets have been delivered.

At José María Vargas Sports Centre, a team of 12 professionals provided 290 health and mental health consultations, including dental care, internal medicine, paediatrics, gynaecology and obstetrics, psychiatry and psychology.

Registration continued at César Nieves Stadium, covering 489 families and 1,479 individuals, and at Playa Grande, covering 54 families and 160 individuals. Progress was also made on the Rapid Needs Assessment and on information management support to the Infrastructure and Temporary Accommodation Working Group.

**IOM Planned Response**

IOM will continue focusing on the improvement and management of transitory camps, WASH, health and MHPSS, protection, registration, needs assessments, mobility monitoring and inter-agency coordination.

Additional funding would enable IOM to scale up shelter assistance, essential items, early recovery, protection, health and mental health, data, DTM and coordination support.

reports.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #10 (9 de julio de 2026)
reports.body_text:
El décimo Reporte de Situación presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela al 9 de julio. También incluye las prioridades del Llamamiento de Fondos de la OIM para ampliar la asistencia urgente.

**Aspectos destacados**

En La Guaira, la OIM y sus socios reforzaron la asistencia en campamentos transitorios. En el Estadio César Nieves continuaron adecuando espacios y distribuyeron lonas y sets de cocina, mientras que en el Polideportivo José María Vargas ampliaron la atención con servicios de odontología y psiquiatría, alcanzando 290 consultas de salud y salud mental.

A la fecha, la OIM ha alcanzado a 4.526 personas únicas mediante 7.273 asistencias y servicios de distribución, principalmente en salud, alojamiento y coordinación de sitios, y protección.

La OIM mantiene su Llamamiento de Fondos por USD 98 millones para asistir a 850.000 personas y apoyar a 140 entidades entre julio y diciembre de 2026.

**Actividades de la OIM**

La OIM continúa apoyando campamentos transitorios priorizados en La Guaira, incluidos el Estadio César Nieves, el Polideportivo José María Vargas y Playa Grande, mediante coordinación de sitios, alojamiento, registro, WASH, salud y salud mental, protección y gestión de información.

En el Estadio César Nieves, se distribuyeron 341 lonas plásticas y 334 sets de cocina. A la fecha, se han entregado 830 lonas y 825 sets de cocina.

En el Polideportivo José María Vargas, un equipo de 12 profesionales brindó 290 consultas de salud y salud mental, incluidas atenciones de odontología, medicina interna, pediatría, ginecología y obstetricia, psiquiatría y psicología.

El registro continuó en el Estadio César Nieves, con 489 familias y 1.479 personas, y en Playa Grande, con 54 familias y 160 personas. También se avanzó en la Evaluación Rápida de Necesidades y en el apoyo de gestión de información al Grupo de Trabajo de Infraestructura y Alojamientos Temporales.

**Respuesta planificada de la OIM**

La OIM continuará enfocándose en la adecuación y gestión de campamentos transitorios, WASH, salud y SMAPS, protección, registro, evaluaciones de necesidades, seguimiento de la movilidad y coordinación interagencial.

El financiamiento adicional permitiría ampliar la asistencia de alojamiento, artículos esenciales, recuperación temprana, protección, salud y salud mental, datos, DTM y apoyo a la coordinación.

reports.title: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 10 de julio 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**CIFRAS CLAVE**

- 3,9K personas fallecidas tras dos poderosos terremotos que sacudieron Venezuela el 24 de junio
- 7,1K personas desplazadas debido a la violencia en el departamento de Ouest de Haití desde el 1 de julio
- 4M de personas podrían necesitar asistencia alimentaria entre junio y enero en Colombia

**VENEZUELA: TERREMOTO**

Más de dos semanas después de los terremotos de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5 del 24 de junio en la región centro-norte de Venezuela, las autoridades informan de 3.889 personas fallecidas, 16.740 heridas y 6.462 rescatadas, con más de 1.100 réplicas registradas. Al 9 de julio, 87 campamentos transitorios siguen brindando apoyo a 16.891 personas en Caracas, La Guaira y Miranda. Los equipos internacionales de búsqueda y rescate urbano han comenzado a desmovilizarse mientras las autoridades nacionales de Protección Civil asumen las operaciones restantes. Tras visitar las comunidades afectadas y reunirse con socios humanitarios nacionales e internacionales, el Subsecretario General de las Naciones Unidas para Asuntos Humanitarios y Coordinador del Socorro de Emergencia, Tom Fletcher, anunció un llamamiento por 298 millones de dólares adicionales para cubrir las necesidades de 1,3 millones de personas en los próximos seis meses.

Las necesidades prioritarias siguen concentradas en alojamiento, salud, agua, saneamiento e higiene (WASH), protección, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial. Save the Children ha expresado preocupación por el bienestar de los aproximadamente 680.000 niñas y niños afectados, cuyos padres y psicólogos informan de signos de angustia aguda. El último análisis del Clúster de Protección, liderado por ACNUR, también señala un aumento de los riesgos de separación familiar, violencia de género y exclusión de la asistencia entre menores, mujeres, personas mayores y personas con discapacidad, impulsados por alojamientos superpoblados, redes de apoyo familiares y comunitarias interrumpidas, y brechas en los servicios para quienes se alojan informalmente fuera de los campamentos designados. A medida que la fase de emergencia va llegando a su fin, los actores humanitarios están priorizando la ampliación del acceso y fortalecer la capacidad para identificar y responder a estos riesgos en el futuro.

[Apoya aquí al Fondo Humanitario Venezolano](https://crisisrelief.un.org/en/donate-venezuela-crisis)

Para más información, visita: [ReliefWeb Response](https://response.reliefweb.int/es/venezuela/terremoto-junio-2026)

**HAITÍ: VIOLENCIA Y DESPLAZAMIENTO**

Dos oleadas separadas de violencia armada en el departamento Ouest de Haití desplazaron a unas 7.168 personas durante la primera semana de julio. Los enfrentamientos del 1 de julio en las localidades de Pinso y Grand-État, en la comuna de Ganthier, desplazaron a 1.328 personas (262 hogares), todas las cuales se refugiaron con familias de acogida dentro del municipio. En Kenscoff, los ataques que comenzaron la noche del 4 al 5 de julio y se extendieron el 8 de julio desplazaron a 5.840 personas (1.836 hogares). La violencia, que resultó en pérdida de vidas, incendios de viviendas y secuestros, también obligó al cierre de tres sitios preexistentes, desplazando a personas que ya se encontraban desplazadas. La mayoría se aloja con familias de acogida, mientras que el 14% se ha trasladado a dos sitios. El incidente supone el mayor desplazamiento de la zona desde febrero de 2025.

**COLOMBIA: SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA**

Una combinación de choques meteorológicos, inseguridad localizada y presiones sobre los precios están impulsando la inseguridad alimentaria en algunas partes de Colombia. Según el último informe de FEWS NET, se prevé que los niveles de Crisis (Fase 3 de la CIF) de inseguridad alimentaria persistan hasta enero de 2027 en los departamentos de La Guajira y Chocó. En La Guajira, las condiciones de El Niño que se están desarrollando agravan los impactos de la sequía en el ganado y los cultivos, mientras que, en Chocó, el riesgo persistente de inundaciones y la inseguridad continúan interrumpiendo el transporte fluvial y el acceso a los mercados, especialmente en la subregión de Baudó. Se prevé que la población que necesita asistencia humanitaria alimentaria en el país aumente gradualmente hasta situarse entre 4,0 y 4,99 millones de personas, identificándose a los hogares rurales pobres, indígenas, afrocolombianos, migrantes venezolanos y de la economía informal urbana como las poblaciones que suscitan mayor preocupación.

reports.title: Latin America & The Caribbean Weekly Situation Update as of 10 July 2026
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**KEY FIGURES**

- 3.9K people dead after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela on 24 June
- 7.1K people displaced due to violence in Haiti’s Ouest department since 1 July
- 4M people may require food assistance between June-January in Colombia

**VENEZUELA: EARTHQUAKE**

More than two weeks after the 24 June magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 earthquakes in Venezuela’s north-central region, authorities report 3,889 people dead, 16,740 injured, and 6,462 rescued, with more than 1,100 aftershocks recorded. As of 9 July, 87 transitional camps remain supporting 16,891 people across Caracas, La Guaira and Miranda. International Urban Search and Rescue teams have begun demobilizing as national Civil Protection authorities take over remaining operations. Following visits to affected communities and meetings with national and international humanitarian partners, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher announced an appeal for an additional US$298 million to meet the needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

Priority needs remain concentrated in shelter, health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection, mental health and psychosocial support. Save the Children has raised concerns about the wellbeing of the roughly 680,000 affected children, with parents and psychologists reporting signs of acute distress. The UNHCR-led Protection Cluster’s latest analysis also points to heightened risks of family separation, gender-based violence, and exclusion from assistance among children, women, older persons, and people with disabilities, driven by overcrowded shelters, disrupted family and community support networks, and service gaps for those sheltering informally outside designated camps. As the emergency phase winds down, humanitarian actors are prioritizing expanded access and stronger capacity to identify and respond to these risks going forward.

[Support the Venezuelan Humanitarian Fund here](https://crisisrelief.un.org/en/donate-venezuela-crisis)

For more information, visit: [ReliefWeb Response](https://response.reliefweb.int/es/venezuela/terremoto-junio-2026)

**HAITI: VIOLENCE & DISPLACEMENT**

Two separate waves of armed violence in Haiti’s Ouest Department displaced an estimated 7,168 people over the first week of July. Clashes on 1 July in the localities of Pinso and Grand-État, Ganthier commune, displaced 1,328 people (262 households), all of whom took refuge with host families within the municipality. In Kenscoff, attacks beginning the night of 4-5 July and spreading on 8 July displaced 5,840 people (1,836 households). The violence, which resulted in loss of life, house burnings and kidnappings, also forced three pre-existing sites to close, displacing people previously displaced. The majority are sheltering with host families while 14 per cent moved into two sites. The incident marks the area’s largest displacement event since February 2025.

**COLOMBIA: FOOD SECURITY**

A combination of weather shocks, localized insecurity and price pressures are driving food insecurity in parts of Colombia. According to FEWS NET’s latest outlook, crisis (IPC Phase 3) levels of food insecurity are expected to persist through January 2027 in the departments of La Guajira and Chocó. In La Guajira, developing El Niño conditions are worsening drought impacts on livestock and crops, while in Chocó, persistent flood risk and insecurity continue to disrupt river transport and market access, particularly in the Baudó subregion. The population requiring humanitarian food assistance across the country is expected to rise gradually to between 4.0 and 4.99 million people, with poor rural, Indigenous, Afro-Colombian, Venezuelan migrant, and informal urban households identified as populations of highest concern.

reports.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Private Sector Contributions Snapshot (As of 9 July 2026)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
This snapshot provides an overview of the private sector humanitarian response to the June 2026 earthquakes in Venezuela.

As of 9 July 2026, businesses and private foundations have mobilized \*US$ 32.9 million\* in support of affected communities and humanitarian partners. This response, tracked by the OCHA-UNDP Connecting Business Initiative (CBi), includes both cash contributions and in-kind support, such as critical relief supplies and heavy machinery for search and rescue operations.

**Key Highlights**

- **Total Resources Mobilized:** US$ 32.9 million
- **Private Sector Partners:** 27
- **Recipient Organizations:** 14

This document outlines the contribution modalities, highlights featured private sector commitments, and lists the partners currently supporting the humanitarian efforts

reports.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: UN Women Flash Update (Reporting period: June 25 – July 6, 2026)
reports.body_text:
This humanitarian update examines the differentiated impact of the earthquakes in Venezuela on women and girls and identifies the key priorities for integrating the gender dimension into the humanitarian response. The report highlights risks such as gender-based violence, the increased burden of unpaid care work, barriers to accessing health services, and the impacts on mental health and livelihoods.

It also outlines the actions led by UN Women in collaboration with women-led organizations, the United Nations system, and other partners, and calls for strengthened funding and coordination to support an inclusive recovery that addresses the specific needs of women and girls.

To learn more about UN Women's response, please visit [Venezuela Earthquakes — Humanitarian Update | Publications | UN Women – Americas and the Caribbean](https://lac.unwomen.org/en/digital-library/publications/2026/07/terremotos-flash-update-venezuela-2026)

reports.title: La OIM refuerza la respuesta a los terremotos en Venezuela con un puente aéreo con suministros de emergencia
reports.body_text:
**Ginebra/Caracas, 10 de julio de 2026** – La Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) ha establecido un puente aéreo de suministros de emergencia para apoyar a las comunidades afectadas en Venezuela tras los devastadores terremotos del 24 de junio de 2026, que causaron daños generalizados y generaron necesidades humanitarias urgentes.

"Para las familias que enfrentan las consecuencias de un terremoto, recibir asistencia en las primeras fases —así como el momento en que se presta— puede marcar una gran diferencia en su capacidad de recuperación", afirmó Kim Eling, Director Superior de Estrategia y Relaciones Externas de la OIM. "Nuestra alianza con DHL demuestra cómo la colaboración estratégica con el sector privado puede ayudar a las organizaciones humanitarias a proporcionar asistencia humanitaria esencial de manera más rápida, garantizando que las comunidades afectadas reciban el apoyo que necesitan en los momentos más críticos".

El cargamento humanitario fue transportado desde el centro de almacenamiento global de la OIM en Panamá hasta Caracas a través de un vuelo de asistencia humanitaria operado por DHL. El Equipo de Respuesta ante Desastres de DHL prestó apoyo en la manipulación del cargamento en los aeropuertos de Panamá y Caracas. El vuelo llegó al Aeropuerto Internacional Simón Bolívar el 7 de julio de 2026, transportando artículos de socorro básicos, entre ellos bidones, lámparas solares y divisores de privacidad para interiores, con el fin de apoyar las operaciones de alojamiento de emergencia.

El traslado fue coordinado en estrecha colaboración entre la OIM, el Gobierno de Venezuela y la Red de Depósitos de Respuesta Humanitaria de las Naciones Unidas (UNHRD) en Panamá, lo que permitió una planificación eficiente, una ejecución ágil y la entrega oportuna de asistencia humanitaria a las comunidades más afectadas.

La OIM expresa su agradecimiento al Equipo de Respuesta a Desastres de DHL por su valioso apoyo logístico, fundamental para la rápida movilización y el transporte de los suministros durante esta emergencia crítica.

Esta operación pone de relieve el compromiso continuo de la OIM con la preparación y la respuesta rápida ante emergencias, así como con la coordinación eficaz de la cadena de suministro humanitaria, mediante el aprovechamiento de alianzas estratégicas y capacidades de preposicionamiento a nivel mundial para entregar asistencia vital a las poblaciones afectadas por crisis.

*Para más información, visite el [Centro de Medios de la OIM](https://www.iom.int/media-inquiries).*

reports.title: IOM Airlifts Core Relief Items to Support the Earthquake Response in Venezuela
reports.body_text:
**Geneva/Caracas, 10 July 2026** – The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has airlifted core relief supplies to support affected communities in Venezuela following the devastating earthquake on 24 June 2026, which caused widespread damage and urgent humanitarian needs.

“For families dealing with the aftermath of an earthquake, whether and when they receive initial assistance can make a big difference for how they are able to recover,” said Kim Eling, IOM Senior Director for Strategy and External Engagement. “Our partnership with DHL demonstrates how strategic collaboration with the private sector can help humanitarian organizations deliver essential assistance more quickly, ensuring affected communities receive the support they need when every moment counts.”

The humanitarian cargo was transported from IOM’s global stock hub in Panama to Caracas through a humanitarian aid flight operated by DHL. DHL’s Disaster Response Team supported in handling the cargo in Panama and Caracas airport. The flight arrived at Simón Bolívar International Airport on 7 July 2026, carrying essential relief items, including jerry cans, solar lamps, and indoor privacy partitions, to support emergency shelter operations.

The movement was coordinated through close collaboration between IOM, the Government of Venezuela, and the United Nations Humanitarian Response Depot (UNHRD) in Panama. This joint effort enabled efficient planning, rapid execution, and timely delivery of assistance to communities most affected by the earthquake.

IOM sincerely thanks DHL’s Disaster Response Team for its generous in-kind logistics support, which was vital to the rapid mobilization and transport of IOM humanitarian supplies during this critical emergency.

This operation highlights IOM’s continued commitment to preparedness, rapid emergency response, and effective humanitarian supply chain coordination, using strategic partnerships and global prepositioning capacities to deliver life-saving assistance to crisis-affected populations.

*For more information, please visit* [*IOM’s Media Centre*](https://www.iom.int/media-inquiries)*.*

reports.title: L'OIM achemine par voie aérienne des articles de secours essentiels pour soutenir les opérations d'urgence suite aux tremblements de terre au Venezuela
reports.body_text:
**Genève/Caracas, 10 juillet 2026** – L'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) a acheminé par voie aérienne des articles de secours essentiels afin de soutenir les communautés affectées au Venezuela, à la suite des tremblements de terre dévastateurs du 24 juin 2026, qui ont causé des dégâts considérables et engendré des besoins humanitaires urgents.

« Pour les familles confrontées aux conséquences d’un séisme, le fait de recevoir ou non une assistance humanitaire initiale, ainsi que le moment de sa réception, peuvent faire une grande différence dans leur capacité à se reconstruire », a déclaré Kim Eling, Directeur principal chargé de la Stratégie et des relations extérieures de l’OIM. « Notre partenariat avec DHL démontre comment une collaboration stratégique avec le secteur privé peut aider les organisations humanitaires à fournir une assistance humanitaire essentielle plus rapidement, garantissant que les communautés affectées reçoivent le soutien dont elles ont besoin lorsque chaque instant compte. »

La cargaison humanitaire a été transportée depuis le centre mondial de stockage de l'OIM au Panama jusqu'à Caracas par un vol d'aide humanitaire opéré par DHL. L'équipe d'intervention en cas de catastrophe de DHL a assuré la gestion de la cargaison à l'aéroport de Panama et à celui de Caracas. Le vol est arrivé à l'aéroport international Simón Bolívar le 7 juillet 2026, transportant des articles de secours essentiels, notamment des jerricanes, des lampes solaires et des cloisons d'intimité intérieures, afin de soutenir les opérations d'abri d'urgence.

Le transport a été coordonné dans le cadre d'une étroite collaboration entre l'OIM, le Gouvernement du Venezuela et le Dépôt mondial de réponse humanitaire des Nations Unies (UNHRD) à Panama. Cet effort conjoint a permis une planification efficace, une exécution rapide et une livraison en temps opportun de l'assistance humanitaire aux communautés les plus touchées par les tremblements de terre.

L'OIM remercie sincèrement l'équipe d'intervention en cas de catastrophe de DHL pour son généreux soutien logistique en nature, qui a été déterminant pour la mobilisation rapide et le transport des fournitures humanitaires de l'OIM lors de cette urgence critique.

Cette opération illustre l'engagement constant de l'OIM en matière de préparation, d'intervention d'urgence rapide et de coordination efficace de la chaîne d'approvisionnement humanitaire, en s'appuyant sur des partenariats stratégiques et des capacités mondiales de prépositionnement pour acheminer une assistance vitale aux populations touchées par des crises.

*Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter le [Centre médias de l'OIM](https://www.iom.int/media-inquiries).*

reports.title: WFP Venezuela Earthquakes Response Situation Report #04, 9 July 2026
reports.body_text:
**KEY HIGHLIGHTS**

• Since the onset of the emergency, WFP has deployed teams to the affected areas to assess the needs of people impacted by the disaster.

• Based on these findings, WFP identified three ways to support affected populations: providing hot meals in temporary shelters and community kitchens; food baskets to families that retained cooking capacity; and ready-to-eat rations to families that lost all cooking capacity.

• WFP aims to reach up to 500,000 people in shelters during the first three months and has the capacity to scale up assistance to one million people.

reports.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Actualización humanitaria - Periodo de reporte: [25 de junio -06 de julio de 2026]
reports.body_text:
Esta actualización humanitaria analiza cómo los terremotos en Venezuela han afectado de manera diferenciada a las mujeres y las niñas, e identifica las principales prioridades para incorporar la dimensión de género en la respuesta. El documento destaca riesgos como la violencia basada en género, la sobrecarga de los cuidados, las dificultades para acceder a servicios de salud y los impactos en la salud mental y los medios de vida.

Además, presenta las acciones impulsadas por ONU Mujeres junto a organizaciones lideradas por mujeres, el Sistema de las Naciones Unidas y otros socios, y hace un llamado a fortalecer la financiación y la coordinación para garantizar una recuperación inclusiva que responda a las necesidades específicas de mujeres y niñas.

Para conocer más sobre la respuesta de ONU Mujeres, visite: [Terremotos en Venezuela — Actualización humanitaria | Publicaciones | ONU Mujeres – América Latina y el Caribe](https://lac.unwomen.org/es/digital-library/publications/2026/07/terremotos-flash-update-venezuela-2026)

reports.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #2: Earthquakes in Venezuela - 09 July 2026
sources: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia
reports.body_text:
On 6 July (local time), AMDA’s advance team (comprising two physicians from AMDA Peru and a Japanese nurse from the U.S.) conducted medical relief efforts in La Guaira, an area devastated by the recent earthquake in Venezuela. The medical response activities were carried out in collaboration with Cruz Azul USM, a medical organization affiliated with Universidad Santa Maria.

The joint relief team saw around 80 patients during the mission where symptoms such as respiratory tract infections, asthma, and gastrointestinal ailments were commonly observed, in addition to acute hypertension, purulent wounds, and other external injuries.

According to the team, although roads leading to La Guaira from Caracas had been heavily congested in the aftermath of the quake, the situation has improved almost to a normal level. Still, people have been forced to live in damaged houses, makeshift tents, or even outdoors, with ongoing power outages. Lack of access to water also remains a problem for many, contributing to the increasing risks of worsening public hygiene as seen in toilets and washing areas.

Meanwhile, AMDA President Dr. Takushi Sato joined the local team after arriving in Venezuela on 7 July.

By carefully assessing needs on the ground, the AMDA team will continue providing aid to those enduring difficult circumstances.

reports.title: Venezuela Earthquakes: Situation Report #6 (July 9, 2026)
reports.body_text:
Project HOPE is steadily expanding its earthquake response across northern Venezuela, shifting more attention to urgent health needs and the prevention of subsequent public health crises. The team has increased the reach of mobile medical teams; reinforced primary health facilities; broadened water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) efforts; and is expanding mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) to assist additional earthquake-affected communities. Preventing disease outbreaks and maintaining consistent access to care remain central priorities as thousands of people navigate uncertainty while living in temporary settlements or damaged neighborhoods.   
  
**Situation Overview**

Humanitarian needs remain significant as response efforts continue. The death toll has been reported at over 3,800, with over 16,700 injuries, and approximately 17,800 displaced and/or homeless people. While debris removal and structural assessments are progressing, thousands of people remain affected and require humanitarian assistance. Health partners remain concerned about deteriorating sanitation conditions, limited access to clean water, and disruptions to routine healthcare, all of which increase the risk of secondary public health emergencies. Project HOPE’s teams continue to report increased cases of diarrheal disease, skin infections, urinary tract infections, dehydration, and respiratory illnesses, with mental health needs remaining high among families coping with displacement and uncertainty. Rainfall and overcrowded shelters are also creating favorable conditions for the spread of infectious diseases, reinforcing the importance of disease surveillance and WASH interventions.

reports.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #16 (09 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**Situation Report No. 16**  
**Earthquakes in Venezuela**  
**09 July 2026**  
**Time: 9:00 pm**

**Highlights**

- Following the 24 June earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 (18:00 local time), **authorities report more than 1,100 aftershocks.**
- Official toll: **3,889 people dead and 16,740 injured.**
- A total of **6,462 people have been rescued.**
- **Tom Fletcher, the United Nations' humanitarian chief, met with national**  
    **and international humanitarian organizations supporting the earthquake response.**
- An additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response and address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.
- The United Nations system and its partner organizations, in coordination with the Government, are responding with multisectoral actions and will continue to scale up assistance to affected people.

**Situation overview**

Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive high-magnitude earthquakes (7.2 and 7.5) that struck on 24 June (18:00 local time) in the north-central region, with the epicentre located along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Authorities report 1,142 aftershocks.**

More than a week after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of **3,889 people dead, 16,740 injured, and 6,462 rescued** since the onset of the emergency. Authorities also reported that approximately **17,907 people lost their homes.**

The Government response remains focused on search and rescue operations, the preparation and expansion of transitional camps and assistance to affected populations. The United Nations and its partner organizations, in coordination with the authorities, are implementing multisectoral response activities and will continue to scale up assistance to affected people. United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher continued his visit to Venezuela. He met with national and international organizations, as well as other counterparts, to strengthen joint efforts with the sole objective of supporting those most in need.

reports.title: Terremotos en Venezuela: Reporte de situación #16 (09 de julio de 2026, Hora: 09:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
reports.body_text:
**Reporte de situación N.º 16**  
**Terremotos en Venezuela**  
**9 de julio de 2026**  
**Hora: 9:00 pm**

**Destacados**

- Tras los sismos de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5 del 24 de junio (18:00 hora local), **las autoridades reportan más de 1.100 réplicas.**
- Balance oficial: 3.889 personas fallecidas y 16.740 heridas.
- **6.462 personas han sido rescatadas.**
- **Tom Fletcher, jefe humanitario de las Naciones Unidas, se reunió con organizaciones humanitarias nacionales e internacionales que**  
    **apoyan la respuesta a los terremotos**.
- **Se lanzó un llamamiento adicional por US$298 millones para ampliar la respuesta a los terremotos y atender las necesidades de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.**
- El Sistema de Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en

reports.body_text:
Al 7 de julio el gobierno nacional ha reportado 3.685 personas fallecidas, 16.740 heridos, 6.462 personas rescatadas y 25.970 pacientes atendidos tras la contingencia, según el Parte Oficial del Gobierno. Se han registrado 1.076 réplicas desde el evento inicial, con una tendencia decreciente en frecuencia y magnitud.

El Clúster de Salud como canal de articulación con el Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud (MPPS) para centralizar la información y la ayuda internacional, la cual asciende a más de 707 mil toneladas.

Se han desplegado 29.567 efectivos nacionales y 4.338 rescatistas internacionales.

Un total de 87 campamentos transitorios se encuentran asignados a nivel nacional (Caracas 39, La Guaira 26, Miranda 22), con una capacidad instalada de 20.227 y 14.634 personas alojadas, según el balance de la Vicepresidencia Social (7 de julio). De estos, el Clúster de Salud monitorea directamente los centros de la Gran Caracas, Miranda y La Guaira y ha realizado visitas en terreno a algunos de ellos.

Una misión exploratoria conjunta (MPPS, UNICEF, Clúster de Salud y GTT SMAPS) al campamento Parque del Oeste / Liceo Miguel Antonio Caro caracterizó una población de aproximadamente 6.102 personas, incluidos 800–1.000 niños, niñas y adolescentes y 260 mujeres embarazadas, e identificó brechas agudas en agua segura, SMAPS, tamizaje nutricional y equipos de protección personal. Así como, el campamento ubicado en la Escuela Gran Colombia, donde al momento de la visita tenía una población de 1.200 personas albergadas, se encontraba coordinado por el poder popular y Ministerios del estado.

reports.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #9 (8 de julio de 2026)
reports.body_text:
El noveno Reporte de Situación presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela al 8 de julio. También incluye las prioridades del Llamamiento de Fondos de la OIM para ampliar la asistencia urgente.

**Aspectos destacados**

La OIM lanzó un Llamamiento de Fondos de USD 98 millones para asistir a 850.000 personas y 140 entidades entre julio y diciembre de 2026, priorizando alojamiento, recuperación temprana, salud, WASH, protección, datos, DTM y coordinación.

En el Estadio César Nieves, se reanudó el registro, con 20 nuevas familias registradas, alcanzando un total de 482 familias, equivalentes a 1.479 personas. En el Polideportivo José María Vargas, el Equipo Médico de Emergencia de la OIM brindó 132 consultas de salud y salud mental.

A la fecha, la OIM ha alcanzado a 4.011 personas únicas con 6.713 asistencias y servicios de distribución, principalmente en salud, alojamiento y protección.

**Actividades de la OIM**

La OIM continúa apoyando campamentos transitorios priorizados en La Guaira, incluidos el Estadio César Nieves, el Polideportivo José María Vargas y Playa Grande, mediante coordinación de sitio, registro, WASH, protección, salud y coordinación interagencial.

En el Estadio César Nieves, continuaron el registro y la coordinación de la distribución de alimentos, mientras que las mejoras WASH avanzaron con la señalización de baños por sexo y la instalación de duchas. En el Polideportivo José María Vargas, se brindaron 132 consultas médicas y de SMAPS.

Las actividades de protección incluyeron seis casos asistidos mediante triaje de protección, sensibilización sobre PEAS, apoyo psicosocial, análisis de riesgo de explotación y abuso sexual, y colocación de materiales informativos sobre PEAS en áreas clave del campamento.

A la fecha, se han movilizado seis vuelos con carga humanitaria, incluidos cinco enviados por DHR del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos en coordinación con la OIM, y un vuelo con suministros de la OIM desde Panamá, con apoyo de DHL.

**Respuesta planificada de la OIM**

La OIM continuará enfocándose en la coordinación y gestión de sitios, registro, WASH, salud y SMAPS, protección, recopilación de datos, DTM y coordinación interagencial en campamentos transitorios priorizados y comunidades afectadas.

El financiamiento adicional a través del Llamamiento de Fondos de USD 98 millones de la OIM permitiría ampliar la asistencia de alojamiento de emergencia, la entrega de artículos esenciales, el apoyo a la recuperación temprana, los servicios de protección, la atención de salud y salud mental, el monitoreo de movilidad y la gestión de información.

reports.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #9 (8 July 2026)
reports.body_text:
The ninth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela as of 8 July. It also includes IOM’s Flash Appeal funding priorities to scale up urgent assistance.

**Highlights**

IOM launched a USD 98 million Appeal to assist 850,000 people and 140 entities between July and December 2026, prioritizing shelter, early recovery, health, WASH, protection, data, DTM and coordination.

At César Nieves Stadium, registration resumed, with 20 new families registered, bringing the total to 482 families, or 1,479 people. At José María Vargas Sports Complex, IOM’s Emergency Medical Team provided 132 health and mental health consultations.

To date, IOM has reached 4,011 unique individuals with 6,713 assistance and distribution services, mainly in health, shelter and protection.

**IOM activities**

IOM continues supporting prioritized transitory camps in La Guaira, including César Nieves Stadium, José María Vargas Sports Complex and Playa Grande, with site coordination, registration, WASH, protection, health and inter-agency coordination.

At César Nieves Stadium, registration and food distribution coordination continued, while WASH improvements advanced through toilet signage by sex and shower installation. At José María Vargas Sports Complex, 132 medical and MHPSS consultations were provided.

Protection activities included six cases assisted through protection triage, PSEA sensitization, psychosocial support, SEA risk analysis and placement of PSEA information materials in key camp areas.

Six humanitarian cargo flights have been mobilized to date, including five sent by DHR of the Government of the United States in coordination with IOM, and one flight with IOM supplies from Panama, supported by DHL.

**IOM planned response**

IOM will continue focusing on site coordination and management, registration, WASH, health and Mental Health, protection, data collection, DTM and inter-agency coordination in prioritized transitory camps and affected communities.

Additional funding through IOM’s USD 98 million Appeal would enable the scale-up of emergency shelter assistance, core relief items, early recovery support, protection services, health and mental health care, mobility monitoring and information management.

reports.title: “They’re flinching at the slightest noise” - Children’s mental wellbeing at stake two weeks on from devastating earthquake
reports.body_text:
**Caracas, 9 July 2026 –** Children are showing signs of mental distress in the wake of last month’s devastating earthquakes in Venezuela, with parents and psychologists reporting children flinching at the slightest noise, finding it difficult to sleep, and showing more signs of irritability and aggression.

Children who have undergone such stressful experiences will often show their stress through behaviour changes and need support to recover, said Save the Children.

Save the Children has established safe spaces for children within the earthquake zone where families can bring their children to play and regain a sense of normalcy and strengthen their resilience, while also being assessed for more severe psychosocial distress or other protection concerns.

Counsellors at these spaces have reported some children are showing signs of acute distress including anger, while children as young as seven or eight are saying they are scared of what the future holds. Some parents have told our staff that their children now become anxious when they see the cracks in the ground, while others are struggling to sleep at night and are flinching when they hear loud sounds such as rumbles of thunder.

Some older children told Save the Children staff that they had to protect and rescue younger family members while they escaped from the earthquake, despite feeling deeply scared themselves, and continue to carry this anxiety with them.

Around 1.8 million people including about 680,000 children have been impacted by the earthquakes that struck Venezuela two weeks ago, many of whom witnessed their friends and family members die before their eyes, with mental and health and psychosocial support identified by the UN and NGOs as one of the key needs facing affected people. \[1\]

Children who have experienced extremely distressing events are at risk of long-lasting impacts for months or even years to come unless they receive mental health and psychosocial support at the onset of the distressful event, said Save the Children.

**Two-year-old Daisy\*** was with her parents when the earthquake struck their home in Caracas. When Daisy stopped eating after the earthquake, **her mother Yusmary\*, 24,** brought her to Save the Children’s mobile health clinic, run by local partner Paluz. Yusmary said that Daisy will now only breastfeed for comfort and will only eat a few spoonfuls of solid food if she is extremely hungry.

**Yusmary said:** *“Before the earthquake, \[Daisy\] used to eat normally, just fine. But after the earthquake, she became like this. When she sees cracks on the floor, she starts crying and screaming. Then she calls me and says, "Mom, look at the floor!"*

**Isabel\*,** a psychologist working with Save the Children said: *“In our safe spaces where children come to play and receive support, we are seeing children who are scared about what the future holds. They are telling us things such as ‘my parents worked so hard to have a house, and now we have nothing.’ Children as young as seven or eight are deeply worried about how they're going to rebuild their lives.*

*“Our safe spaces allow children to express themselves in a safe and supportive environment which is vital since some children are telling our teams that they are reluctant to express their fears at home, as they see their parents and caregivers upset and worried”.*

**Fatima Andraca, Save the Children’s Country Director in Venezuela said:**

*“Many children in Venezuela have experienced extremely distressing events that no child should ever have to see. They have witnessed their friends and family members die before their eyes, while others continue to live with the uncertainty of not knowing where their loved ones are. Thousands of children are sheltering in tents in the streets where their daily routines and sense of security have been ripped away.*

*“Protection and psychosocial support are urgent priorities for children. With so many people dead, injured or missing, and so many families uprooted from their homes, children need both immediate and long-term support to ensure that this devastating disaster does not cause long lasting mental harm. With the right help, most children psychologically impacted by the earthquakes will eventually be able to recover.”*

Save the Children is on the ground in Venezuela, working with authorities and local partners and will be providing primary healthcare through mobile clinics, distributing hygiene and shelter kits, clean water and essential supplies. Save the Children is also running safe spaces where children can access mental health support and continue learning while schools remain closed, and where those with more significant needs can be referred for individual support.

Save the Children is an independent, impartial child rights organisation, working in Venezuela since 2019. Since the humanitarian crisis started to rapidly deteriorate a few years ago, Save the Children has been scaling up its response through local partners to support the increasing number of children in need.

\*Names changed for anonymity.

**We have multimedia content available here:**

Jose\* (11):

[www.contenthubsavethechildren.org/Package/2O4C2SPUFZ7K](http://www.contenthubsavethechildren.org/Package/2O4C2SPUFZ7K)

Yusmary\* (24) and Daisy\* (2): [www.contenthubsavethechildren.org/Package/2O4C2SPUFF22](http://www.contenthubsavethechildren.org/Package/2O4C2SPUFF22)

\[1\] [https://reliefweb.int/report/venezuela-bolivarian-republic/venezuela-protection-situation-update-3-earthquake-response](https://reliefweb.int/report/venezuela-bolivarian-republic/venezuela-protection-situation-update-3-earthquake-response)

reports.title: Venezuela Earthquake: Flash Update #2 (9th July 2026)
reports.body_text:
Two weeks after the 24 June seismic doublet (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5, 39 seconds apart), Venezuela's emergency has shifted from acute search and rescue into sustained, multi-sector humanitarian operations, even as rescuers occasionally still find survivors and already-weakened buildings continue to collapse.  

The official death toll stands at 3,535, with 16,740 people injured and nearly 18,000 displaced. Authorities now report more than 940 aftershocks. Buildings damaged are reported between 856 (government) and 2,501 (OCHA/ partner tracking), including 190 confirmed collapses.  

More than 55,000 people remain unaccounted for on the national missing-persons platform, of which 123 are children. Authorities report 80 operational transitional camps supporting the displaced population.  

Independent satellite-based analysis (ANOVA Policy Research, with Microsoft AI for Good) suggests population exposure in La Guaira's coastal corridor may be up to three times higher than official figures capture, due to outdated census frameworks and under-counted floating population. Of an estimated 403,784 residents across seven La Guaira parishes, roughly 73,500 lived in structures with observable damage, and 37,600 in structures with severe damage or collapse — the group most likely to need transitional or permanent housing.  

The UNDRR assessment estimates approximately USD 37 billion in direct damage economy-wide, of which roughly USD 24 billion is concentrated in housing, businesses, schools, hospitals, and public facilities, alongside a separate preliminary UNDP estimate of USD 6.7 billion, equivalent to 6% of GDP.

reports.title: Venezuela Earthquakes leave children at greater risk of violence
reports.body_text:
9 July 2026 The earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June have left children increasingly vulnerable to trafficking, sexual exploitation, violence and other forms of abuse, as families struggle to recover from the devastation.

### Trafficking networks target children in emergencies

Yesica Serrano, Regional Child Protection in Humanitarian Action Adviser at Plan International, speaking from Caracas stressed that criminal trafficking networks often seek to take advantage of the chaos that follows emergencies, targeting girls and boys who have been separated from their families, lost their care givers or have missing relatives or who are otherwise left vulnerable by the crisis.

“During emergencies, the protective care environment for children weakens. Caregivers are under immense stress, looking for ways to cope with their situation, may lose a certain level of alertness and vigilance over the care of children. And it is in these lapses that trafficking networks and other perpetrators of abuse take advantage of these moments of vulnerability to target and recruit children,” said Serrano from Caracas.

As an aggravating factor, recruitment of children through social media is common in Latin America, and during emergencies, when children are more connected online and caregivers are focused on rebuilding their lives and other basic needs, attention to the content children consume decreases, which increases the risk of exposure to harmful content.

### Children vulnerable to multiple forms of abuse

Family separation is among the most significant child protection risks following a disaster. When caregivers have died, are hospitalised, or lose contact with children during evacuation children can be left without the care and protection they need. Children who are alone or whose family support networks have been disrupted face heightened risks of trafficking and sexual exploitation.

Adolescent girls and boys are more exposed to child labour, trafficking for the purposes of sexual exploitation, and recruitment by criminal groups, through coercion or false promises, presenting themselves as an alternative solution to meet their needs.

“Emergencies do not affect all children equally. Girls and adolescent girls face increased risks of sexual exploitation, violence and child labour, particularly linked to domestic work, while adolescents in general are more exposed to the possible risk of recruitment by criminal groups.” Said Carmen Elena Alemán, Regional Director for Plan International in Latin America and the Caribbean.

### How Plan works to keep children safe

Plan International works to prevent these risks alongside its partner organisations, providing group-based psychosocial support to caregivers to prevent violence and strengthen protective family environments, and working directly with children to reduce their risk factors for violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect, and to support their psycho-emotional recovery.

In addition, we are distributing hygiene kits and dignity kits as well as essential household items, providing safe spaces and psychosocial support in communities across 2 affected states, and conducting emergency education and primary health care activities, with a special focus on girls and adolescents.

The organisation calls on various stakeholders to ensure that the humanitarian response in Venezuela incorporates child protection measures from the very beginning: family tracing and reunification processes in coordination with the relevant authorities; strengthened oversight in shelters and collective housing sites; and accessible reporting mechanisms adapted to children’s needs.

[Venezuela earthquake appeal](https://plan-international.org/get-involved/venezuela-earthquake-appeal/)

reports.title: Situational Report - Response to Venezuela Earthquakes (July 8th, 2026)
reports.body_text:
**Highlights**

• The humanitarian crisis continues to evolve following the twin earthquakes of 24 June. According to OCHA (7 July), 3,685 people have died, 16,740 have been injured, more than 1,000 aftershocks have been recorded and 6,462 people have been rescued, with La Guaira remaining the hardest-hit state. Authorities also report that 17,907 people have been left without housing, increasing humanitarian needs across affected communities.

• The response is progressively shifting from life-saving search and rescue to sustained humanitarian assistance, with temporary camps expanding and growing needs in health, shelter, safe water, sanitation, protection and education.  
Humanitarian actors continue scaling up multisectoral support.

• Child protection concerns continue to intensify. Children remain at heightened risk of family separation, violence, psychosocial distress and disrupted education, reinforcing the need for specialised protection and mental health services.

• Assessments continue to confirm a severe humanitarian crisis, including widespread housing destruction, damaged public infrastructure, overwhelmed health services and critical water and sanitation needs. Authorities report 856 affected buildings, including 190 collapsed structures, while preliminary estimates place direct physical damage at USD 37 billion.

• Preliminary estimates indicate USD 37 billion in direct physical damage, underscoring that humanitarian needs will extend beyond emergency relief into recovery, reconstruction and restoration of essential services.

• Plan International with partners has already reached more than 1,635 people across Distrito Capital and Miranda with psychosocial support, primary health care and emergency relief items, while continuing to scale up operations.

reports.title: Venezuela Protection Situation Update #3 - Earthquake Response
reports.body_text:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

On the 24th of June 2026, two earthquakes of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitudes affected the centre-north of Venezuela, with particularly severe consequences in the states of La Guaira and Grand Caracas. After 12 days, the emergency continues to evolve in a context marked by internal displacement, temporary shelter arrangements for affected populations in formal or informal collective spaces, persistent disruptions in access to services, and growing demand for humanitarian assistance and protection mechanisms.

The available information shows that protection needs continue to rise among the population affected by the earthquakes. In addition, the effects of the emergency are not strictly limited to the areas directly impacted, as population displacements have been observed toward host communities and other states in the country, including Bolívar, Delta Amacuro, Anzoátegui, Sucre, Zulia, Táchira, and Apure. The loss of homes, displacement, stays in temporary government-managed shelters and informal accommodation sites, as well as the disruption or weakening of family, community, institutional, and protection networks, have increased exposure to protection risks and reduced the coping capacity of affected communities.

Assessments conducted identify significant concerns related to mental health and psychosocial support needs, family separation, inadequate privacy and security in accommodation facilities, and the loss of personal documentation, which may affect access to assistance and essential services. These risks disproportionately affect children and adolescents, women, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other individuals with specific protection needs. In this context, the sector’s priorities continue to focus on strengthening protection mechanisms for the most vulnerable populations, increasing access to specialised services, and helping ensure that affected people can access humanitarian assistance and available services safely and with dignity.
